settings.label: Theme
settings.desc: Changes the whole app's look and colors instantly - no restart needed. Picks one of eight looks: Friendly, Glass, Retro, and Basic, each in dark and light; the Theme Mode control (Light/Dark/Auto) decides whether the dark or light look of the chosen family is shown.

settings.label: Theme Mode
settings.desc: Picks light, dark, or follow-your-computer coloring for the selected theme family. Auto follows the operating system appearance (prefers-color-scheme) and switches live when the OS setting changes.

settings.label: Light Or Dark (Basic Theme)
settings.desc: Picks light, dark, or follow-your-computer coloring when the Basic Modern theme is active. Switches live, no restart. (Superseded by general.visual.theme-mode)

settings.label: Preview Themes Before Applying
settings.desc: Shows what a theme looks like while you browse, then snaps back if you don't apply it. Turn off to switch instantly.

settings.label: Glass Background
settings.desc: What shows behind the glass panels in Glass themes: Mesh is a slowly drifting color gradient, Depth adds floating soft shapes with gentle parallax, Minimal keeps a calm flat backdrop. Applies instantly.

settings.label: Glass Transparency
settings.desc: How see-through glass panels are. Every theme keeps a readability floor - dark glass never drops below 0.35, light glass never below 0.45 - so text stays legible. Only adjustable while a Glass theme is active.

settings.label: Retro Effects
settings.desc: Adds the pixel grid, paper texture, and scanline overlays on Retro themes. Turn off for a cleaner, flatter look.

settings.label: UI Scale
settings.desc: Makes everything in the app bigger or smaller. Handy on high-resolution screens or if text feels cramped.

settings.label: Text Size
settings.desc: Base size for text across the app. Bump it up if you find yourself leaning toward the screen.

settings.label: Interface Density
settings.desc: How tightly packed the interface is. Auto adapts to your window size, Comfortable gives everything room to breathe, Compact fits more on screen. Applies instantly.

settings.label: Reduce Animations
settings.desc: Calms the interface: entrance animations, hover sheens, and background drift stop, while the app keeps working exactly the same. Applies instantly - helpful if movement is distracting or causes discomfort.

settings.label: Chat Layout
settings.desc: Where the assistant chat lives: Docked to the right edge of the window, Overlay sliding above your work, or Detached as its own floating window. Applies instantly.

settings.label: High Contrast Mode
settings.desc: Boosts color contrast to meet accessibility standards. Works with the Basic theme; makes text and edges easier to see.

settings.label: App Font
settings.desc: Choose the retro display fonts or your computer's standard fonts. Changing this restarts the app.

settings.label: Manage Custom Themes
settings.desc: Create, import, or export your own theme files, or open the themes folder. Broken theme files are skipped with a warning.

settings.label: Custom Theme Starting Point
settings.desc: Which built-in theme your custom theme inherits from. Any colors you don't set fall back to this base.

settings.label: Pixel Grid Strength
settings.desc: How visible the retro pixel-grid overlay is. Lower it if the texture feels too busy; zero hides it.

settings.label: Scanline Strength
settings.desc: How visible the retro scanline overlay is. Lower for subtlety; zero turns scanlines off entirely.

settings.label: Border Width
settings.desc: Thickness of panel and control borders. Retro uses chunky 2px lines; Basic uses thin 1px ones.

settings.label: Corner Roundness
settings.desc: How rounded corners are. Retro is sharp (0px); Basic softens to 4px. Changing theme families restarts the app.

settings.label: Line Spacing
settings.desc: Vertical space between lines of text. Higher values make long text easier to read but show less per screen.

settings.label: Scrollbar Width
settings.desc: How wide scrollbars are. Retro uses styled 12px bars; Basic uses slimmer system-like 8px bars.

settings.label: Padding Scale
settings.desc: Fine-tunes internal spacing inside panels and controls, on top of the Display Density choice.

settings.label: Focus Outline Style
settings.desc: How the keyboard-focus outline looks. High-contrast and color-blind-safe options make it easier to track where you are.

settings.label: Explain Things To Me
settings.desc: Plain-English mode hides jargon and advanced panels; Expert shows every control. Changes wording and detail app-wide.

settings.label: Explain Terms In This Chat
settings.desc: Asks the assistant to define technical terms as it goes, in this chat only. Doesn't change generated documents.

settings.label: Show Tooltips
settings.desc: Shows hover hints on buttons and controls so you can learn what things do without clicking them.

settings.label: Keep Running In System Tray
settings.desc: Closing the window hides the app in the tray instead of quitting, so runs keep going. The tray icon shows activity.

settings.label: Notifications
settings.desc: Master switch for all alerts. Turn off for total quiet — you'll have to check the app yourself for approvals.

settings.label: How Alerts Appear
settings.desc: Choose whether alerts pop up as toasts, banners, or system tray bubbles.

settings.label: Tray Alerts For Big Events
settings.desc: System-tray alerts for the important stuff only: approval requests, run finished, major failures, and rate limits.

settings.label: Sound Effects
settings.desc: Plays short sounds for approvals, completions, and errors. Off by default; hidden if your computer has no audio.

settings.label: Browse & Preview Sounds
settings.desc: Listen to the built-in sound library and test-send alerts to your notification destinations before committing.

settings.label: Send Message Key
settings.desc: Which key sends your chat message. Pick Enter for speed, or Ctrl+Enter to avoid sending half-typed thoughts.

settings.label: Default Assistant Mode
settings.desc: What the assistant starts in: Ask only answers, Agent makes changes, Debug diagnoses, Plan and Deep Plan think first.

settings.label: Follow New Messages
settings.desc: Keeps chat scrolled to the newest message. If you scroll up to read, a jump-to-latest badge appears instead.

settings.label: Unread Message Marker
settings.desc: Shows a sticky marker at the last message you read when you've scrolled away, so you never lose your place.

settings.label: Copy Button On Code Blocks
settings.desc: Puts an always-visible copy button on every code block in chat, so grabbing code takes one click.

settings.label: Edit & Resend Last Message
settings.desc: Lets you fix and resend your most recent chat message instead of retyping it.

settings.label: Question Cards
settings.desc: When the assistant needs answers, it shows tidy cards with options and a free-text box instead of a wall of text.

settings.label: Auto-Save Question Answers
settings.desc: Continuously saves your half-finished answers on question cards, so dismissing a card never loses your typing.

settings.label: Show Context Usage In Chat
settings.desc: Displays how full the assistant's working memory is, with a link to details — useful to know when to start fresh.

settings.label: Show Activity Cards
settings.desc: Shows collapsible cards for commands, web searches, and file edits the assistant performs, so you can see its work.

settings.label: Show File-Reading Activity
settings.desc: Shows routine progress cards while the assistant explores your files. Safety and approval messages always show regardless.

settings.label: Render Diagrams In Chat
settings.desc: Turns Mermaid diagram code into actual flowcharts and graphs inside chat and planning views.

settings.label: Interactive Visuals In Chat
settings.desc: Lets the assistant show small sandboxed interactive widgets (charts, previews) inline. They can't touch your files.

settings.label: Switch Modes By Asking
settings.desc: Lets phrases like 'use plan mode' or 'be a rust engineer' switch modes and personas mid-conversation.

settings.label: Show Helper Agent Details
settings.desc: Always discloses when the assistant spins up helper agents, including their persona, model, and platform.

settings.label: Show Actual Model Used
settings.desc: Tells you when the AI provider or model actually used differs from the one requested, so nothing swaps silently.

settings.label: Image Tools In Message Box
settings.desc: Shows image attach and generation buttons in the message box when the current model supports them.

settings.label: Share From Browser
settings.desc: Lets you click and highlight things in the built-in browser to share as chat context. Nothing is sent until you confirm.

settings.label: Auto-Detect Project Languages
settings.desc: Figures out what languages your project uses, shows badges, and suggests matching tools automatically.

settings.label: Hide Ignored Files
settings.desc: Hides files your project's ignore list excludes (like build output) from the file tree. Off shows them dimmed.

settings.label: Highlight Open File In Tree
settings.desc: Automatically scrolls and expands the file tree to show whichever file you're editing.

settings.label: Search All Settings
settings.desc: Fuzzy-searches every settings row across every tab, including hidden ones (shown as unavailable).

settings.label: Show Where Settings Apply
settings.desc: Labels each setting with its scope (Global, Project, Persona…) and which layer won, so overrides aren't a mystery.

settings.label: Dashboard Widgets
settings.desc: Choose and arrange the widgets on your dashboard. Core widgets stay visible; projects can override the app default.

settings.label: Sidebar Icon Order
settings.desc: Drag to reorder the icons in the left activity bar per project, so your most-used panels sit on top.

settings.label: Panel Position
settings.desc: Whether side panels like Chat and File Manager sit docked to an edge or float as separate windows, per project.

settings.label: Keep Hidden Features Findable
settings.desc: Features hidden when unused stay reachable through settings search, commands, and links — nothing vanishes for good.

settings.label: History Shows
settings.desc: Whether the History view lists only the current project's runs or everything across all projects.

settings.label: History: Approved Items Only
settings.desc: Shows only approved work in History by default; 'All history' expands to drafts and rejected items too.

settings.label: History: Include Archived
settings.desc: Also lists archived runs and plans in History, which can make long lists noisier.

settings.label: Compare History Versions
settings.desc: Opens a side-by-side comparison of two versions: rendered output, source lineage, or manifest views.

settings.label: While The Assistant Is Busy
settings.desc: Steer interrupts the assistant with your new message; Queue holds it until the current step finishes.

settings.label: Max Queued Messages
settings.desc: How many messages can wait in line while the assistant works. A full queue blocks new messages until one clears.

settings.label: Alert Me About
settings.desc: Which severity levels trigger alerts. Fewer levels means fewer interruptions; blocked items always deserve a look.

settings.label: Where Alerts Go
settings.desc: Send alerts beyond the app: Slack, Discord, webhooks, ntfy, Pushover, or Telegram. Credentials stay in the vault.

settings.label: Route Events To Destinations
settings.desc: Pick which kinds of events go to which destination — e.g. approvals to your phone, completions to Slack.

settings.label: Manage Sounds
settings.desc: Upload custom sounds or import packs; files are checked for format, size, and length. Previews play locally only.

settings.label: Assign Sounds To Events
settings.desc: Choose which sound plays for each event type, like a distinct chime for approvals versus errors.

settings.label: Quiet Advisory Alerts After (min)
settings.desc: Advisory warnings hush automatically after things stay stable this long. Urgent and blocked alerts never auto-quiet.

settings.label: Require Reason To Dismiss Alerts
settings.desc: Asks for a short explanation before you can dismiss attention items, creating a paper trail for later.

settings.label: Auto-Explain Grayed-Out Controls
settings.desc: Automatically pops up an explanation when you hit a disabled control. The manual 'Explain this' option always exists.

settings.label: Max Open Editor Tabs
settings.desc: Caps how many files stay open at once; the least-recently-used tab closes when you exceed it. Keeps memory in check.

settings.label: Max Files Listed Per Folder
settings.desc: Caps entries shown per directory in the file tree so giant folders don't freeze the app.

settings.label: When Dropped Files Clash
settings.desc: What happens when a drag-and-drop hits an existing filename: ask you, overwrite, or keep both with a rename.

settings.label: Default Drag-And-Drop Action
settings.desc: Whether dragging files copies or moves them by default. Holding Shift does the opposite.

settings.label: Remember Expanded Folders
settings.desc: Remembers which folders you had open in the file tree for each project between sessions.

settings.label: Auto-Archive Chats After (days)
settings.desc: Automatically archives chat threads untouched for this many days. Zero means never archive automatically.

settings.label: Keep Deleted Chats For (days)
settings.desc: How long deleted chat records are recoverable before they're gone for good.

settings.label: Show Thread Technical Details
settings.desc: Shows session IDs and branch lineage in thread details — useful only when debugging how chats connect to work.

settings.label: Run Graph View
settings.desc: Whether the run graph follows what's happening live or lets you browse a past run's history.

settings.label: Run Graph Detail Level
settings.desc: How much the node graph shows: everything, a simplified view, or grouped by package lanes or seam boundaries.

settings.label: Progress View Layout
settings.desc: Customize which widgets appear on the orchestrator progress view, with a per-project override of the app default.

settings.label: Export History
settings.desc: Exports selected or filtered history rows with their manifests, run through your redaction profile so secrets stay out.

settings.label: Rebuild History Index
settings.desc: Rebuilds the history search index if it goes stale and results look wrong or incomplete.

settings.label: Reset Home Layout
settings.desc: Returns Home panels, docks, terminal placement, and floating bounds to the safe default without closing editor buffers, terminal sessions, Browser state, Dashboard widgets, or chat history. Dual-surface since 2026-08-13: the top-bar Home menu carries a matching Reset Layout row, and both routes run the same layout reset command.

settings.label: Show First-Run Tips
settings.desc: Runs the welcome tour and shows guided tips for newcomers. Turns itself off once done; reset it from Health anytime.

settings.label: Panel To Open On Launch
settings.desc: Which side panel greets you when a project opens — your last-used one, or always the same panel.

settings.label: Remember Window Layout
settings.desc: Restores window size, position, panel widths, and splits exactly as you left them last time.

settings.label: Restore Sessions After A Crash
settings.desc: Brings back your terminals, editors, and chats automatically if the app crashes, so you pick up where you left off.

settings.label: Protect Unsaved Work
settings.desc: Keeps snapshots of unsaved editor changes so a crash can't eat text you hadn't saved yet.

settings.label: Tabs Remembered Between Sessions
settings.desc: How many editor tabs are saved when you quit and reopened next launch; the oldest drop off beyond this.

settings.label: Re-Check Debug Setup On Resume
settings.desc: When resuming a debugging chat, re-verifies the target, logins, and instrumentation are still valid before continuing.

settings.label: AI Provider Connections
settings.desc: Connect, re-check, or disconnect your AI accounts. Everything else needs at least one working connection here.

settings.label: GitHub Connection
settings.desc: Sign in to GitHub so Puppet Master can create branches and pull requests for you. Disconnect removes the saved token.

settings.label: Default Account Per Provider
settings.desc: When a provider has several accounts, this one is used first. Health, cooldowns, and reset times show next to each choice.

settings.label: Account Active
settings.desc: Turn an account off to keep it saved but skip it when choosing who runs your work. Nothing is deleted.

settings.label: Account Nickname
settings.desc: A friendly name so you can tell accounts apart, like 'Work Claude' or 'Personal'.

settings.label: Use This Account Next
settings.desc: Force a specific account for the current or next run — handy when testing or when one account is running low.

settings.label: Claude Sign-in Method
settings.desc: How your Claude account signs in. Subscription and console logins have different limits and billing.

settings.label: Codex Sign-in Type
settings.desc: ChatGPT plan and API key are separate quota pools with separate bills — set up each one you use.

settings.label: Sign-in Method Per Provider
settings.desc: Whether a provider uses an API key, browser login, or its own default. Only methods the provider supports are offered.

settings.label: Auto-Switch Between Accounts
settings.desc: When one account hits its limit, quietly continue on the next one instead of stopping your work.

settings.label: Enable OpenCode
settings.desc: Turn on the OpenCode engine as an extra way to run AI work. Off means its servers and models stay hidden.

settings.label: Add OpenCode Server
settings.desc: Let Puppet Master start and manage a server for you, or attach to one you already run yourself.

settings.label: OpenCode Server Address
settings.desc: Where the OpenCode server lives, like http://127.0.0.1:4096. Wrong address means models never appear.

settings.label: Anthropic API Key
settings.desc: Key for direct Anthropic access and Claude usage reporting. Shown redacted; stored in your keychain, never in config files.

settings.label: OpenAI API Key
settings.desc: Key for OpenAI services, including image generation. Shown redacted in the app.

settings.label: Gemini API Key
settings.desc: Key for Gemini Direct, including media generation. Key-only — no browser login for this route.

settings.label: Cursor API Key
settings.desc: Optional key from cursor.com/dashboard. Browser sign-in is the default and easier route for most people.

settings.label: MiniMax API Key
settings.desc: Key for the MiniMax global image route. The China route is a separate account with its own key.

settings.label: GitHub Access Token
settings.desc: Personal token for GitHub features and Copilot usage stats. Separate from Copilot's own provider sign-in.

settings.label: Allowed GitHub Servers
settings.desc: Whether company-hosted GitHub Enterprise servers may be used, or only github.com. Enterprise repos show as disabled otherwise.

settings.label: GitHub Sign-in Callback Address
settings.desc: Local address used during GitHub browser sign-in. Only this-computer addresses are accepted; public ones are rejected.

settings.label: Where Keys Are Kept
settings.desc: Where each account's secret lives — your system keychain (safest), an environment variable, a file, or the provider's CLI.

settings.label: How Keys Are Sent
settings.desc: The technical way a credential is attached to requests. Only change if a provider's docs tell you to.

settings.label: Account Type
settings.desc: Whether an account is a subscription, API key, browser login, or CLI-managed. Affects how limits and resets are counted.

settings.label: Stick to a Chosen Account
settings.desc: None lets policy pick; Preferred falls back with a logged reason; Required stops work rather than use another account.

settings.label: Requested Account for This Run
settings.desc: Explicitly name the account a run should use, separate from the general binding policy.

settings.label: Account Priority Order
settings.desc: Lower numbers get picked first. Ties go to the account already doing the work, so runs stay stable.

settings.label: Switch Early Before Limits Hit
settings.desc: Move to the next account at a natural break once quota runs low, instead of waiting for a hard stop mid-task.

settings.label: Low-Quota Warning Level
settings.desc: Warn when an account has less than this much quota left, so switches don't surprise you.

settings.label: Auto-Switch Trigger Level
settings.desc: Switch accounts when remaining quota drops below this. Some docs express it as 80% used — same idea, opposite direction.

settings.label: Per-Account Switch Override
settings.desc: Give one account its own switch trigger, different from the global level — useful for small trial accounts.

settings.label: Account Rotation Style
settings.desc: Sticky stays on one account, fallback only moves when forced, round-robin spreads work evenly.

settings.label: Rate-Limit Rest Period
settings.desc: How long an account rests after hitting a rate limit before it's tried again. Provider defaults are usually right.

settings.label: Retries Before Giving Up
settings.desc: How many times a struggling account is retried before it's benched, so one flaky account can't stall everything.

settings.label: Quota Profile
settings.desc: Which provider quota plan an account follows — sets how usage and reset windows are tracked for it.

settings.label: Jobs This Account May Do
settings.desc: Limit an account to certain kinds of work, or block it from some — e.g. keep an expensive account off routine tasks.

settings.label: Google Cloud Project ID
settings.desc: For Gemini accounts: which Google Cloud project gets billed and whose quota applies.

settings.label: Who Gets Billed
settings.desc: Pick the org, team, or personal context charged for this account. Costs are tracked per billing entity.

settings.label: Account Switch History
settings.desc: Read-only log of every automatic account switch and why it happened — good for 'why did my bill change?' questions.

settings.label: OpenCode Server Password
settings.desc: Username and password for reaching the server itself — separate from any AI provider keys inside it.

settings.label: OpenCode Server Controls
settings.desc: Reconnect, restart (managed only), refresh the model list, or detach a server from Puppet Master's control.

settings.label: OpenCode Model List Cache (s)
settings.desc: How long the discovered model list is trusted before re-asking the server. Lower means fresher but chattier.

settings.label: OpenCode CLI Path (Fallback)
settings.desc: Optional path to the OpenCode binary, used only when the direct server connection isn't available.

settings.label: Skip Claude Code Skills in OpenCode
settings.desc: Stops OpenCode loading Claude Code skills on its own. Puppet Master still routes its canonical skills either way.

settings.label: Default Model
settings.desc: The model used when nothing more specific applies — chat, planning, research. Run and persona choices override it.

settings.label: Default AI Provider
settings.desc: Which AI company's service is tried first. Greyed-out entries are disconnected or missing a needed capability.

settings.label: Overseer Model
settings.desc: The planner-in-chief: turns plans into work, supervises runs, and reasons about anything that gets stuck.

settings.label: Worker Model
settings.desc: Does the everyday building work. A solid mid-range model keeps costs sane without hurting quality.

settings.label: Design & Layout Model
settings.desc: Handles visual work — screens, layout, look and feel. Pick a model that's strong at front-end taste.

settings.label: Heavy-Lifting Model
settings.desc: Reserved for the hardest jobs — big cross-project changes and risky reasoning. Usually your most capable model.

settings.label: Auditor Model
settings.desc: Double-checks finished work in an audit-and-repair loop until it's certified or truly blocked. Its provider can differ too.

settings.label: Speed vs Power Preset
settings.desc: A quick lever between fast-and-cheap and slow-and-thorough without changing which model is picked.

settings.label: Thinking Depth
settings.desc: How hard models think before answering. Deeper is smarter but slower and pricier; the app shows what was actually honored.

settings.label: Help & Explain Model
settings.desc: The model behind 'explain this to me' help threads. A cheaper model here keeps learning free-feeling.

settings.label: Provider On/Off
settings.desc: Switch a whole provider off for future runs. Its accounts stay saved and can be switched back on anytime.

settings.label: Goal Mode Worker Model
settings.desc: The model that executes autonomous goal runs. Kept separate from the checker so no one grades their own homework.

settings.label: Goal Mode Checker Model
settings.desc: Verifies and adjudicates goal-run results. Must meet the certification bar or the run blocks — it never just warns.

settings.label: Capability Lane Assignments
settings.desc: Pin each work lane (cheap executor, reviewer, orchestrator, verifier, adjudicator, certifier) to a provider, account, and model.

settings.label: Role Model Policy
settings.desc: Advanced mapping of roles (worker default, planner, evaluator) and provider capability-level defaults, stored apart from the pickers above.

settings.label: Helper Agent Model
settings.desc: Model for spawned helper agents. A helper can never use a bigger budget or model than its parent allows.

settings.label: Helper Agent Thinking Depth
settings.desc: Thinking depth for each helper agent, settled and recorded when its result comes back.

settings.label: Per-Lane AI Platform
settings.desc: Choose a different AI platform for each work lane — seams, packages, lanes, and nodes can each run somewhere else.

settings.label: Per-Lane Model Names
settings.desc: Exact model name for each work lane, in the chosen platform's own format. Leave blank to inherit.

settings.label: Run Execution Role
settings.desc: Which role a run acts as (assistant, interview, orchestrator...). Recorded into attempt and usage history.

settings.label: Provider Try-Order
settings.desc: The order providers are tried when several could do a job. Drag to reorder; applies everywhere for now.

settings.label: Fall Back When Provider Is Down
settings.desc: If your first-choice provider is unavailable, quietly try the next in line instead of failing the run.

settings.label: Auto-Pick Aggressiveness
settings.desc: How boldly the app auto-picks models: conservative never guesses, aggressive chases the cheapest or fastest option.

settings.label: My Custom Presets
settings.desc: Define your own named speed/power presets — each needs a unique name, a model, and an optional description.

settings.label: Hide Built-in Presets
settings.desc: Hide presets you never use from pickers and quick-cycling, so the list only shows what you actually reach for.

settings.label: Model Nicknames
settings.desc: Give models friendly names ('my fast one'). Lookups match nickname first, then exact ID, then display name.

settings.label: Response Randomness
settings.desc: Higher makes answers more varied, lower more predictable. Left at model default unless you have a reason; ignored if unsupported.

settings.label: Word-Choice Focus (Top-p)
settings.desc: Narrows or widens the pool of words a model considers. Leave at model default unless experimenting; skipped if unsupported.

settings.label: Longest Allowed Answer
settings.desc: Caps how much a model can write per reply (Anthropic 64k, OpenAI 32k by default). Per-model overrides are possible.

settings.label: Provider Feature Switches
settings.desc: Turn individual provider features on or off: streaming, tool use, thinking blocks, parallel tools, prefill, image input.

settings.label: Prompt Caching
settings.desc: Reuses repeated context to cut cost and speed things up. Support varies by provider; current state is shown per provider.

settings.label: Caching on Browser Logins
settings.desc: Whether cached-context savings also apply to accounts signed in via browser, not just API keys. Provider-dependent.

settings.label: Gemini Cache Lifetime (min)
settings.desc: How long Gemini keeps cached context alive. Must be above zero; longer saves more on repeated context.

settings.label: Largest Request Size
settings.desc: Provider-specific ceiling on how big a single request may be. Rarely needs touching.

settings.label: System Message Role Name
settings.desc: Whether instructions are sent as 'system' or 'developer' — some OpenAI reasoning models require 'developer'.

settings.label: Extra Provider Options
settings.desc: Raw key-value options passed straight to a provider, for anything without its own switch. Checked against capabilities first.

settings.label: What Actually Ran
settings.desc: Read-only view comparing what you asked for (model, account, effort) with what actually ran, and why they differ.

settings.label: Think Between Tool Steps
settings.desc: Lets the model pause and think between tool calls in chat. Per-thread; the app shows if a provider can't fully honor it.

settings.label: Clean Up on Model Switch
settings.desc: Drops thinking and cache leftovers that a new model can't read when switching mid-run, so switches don't corrupt context.

settings.label: Auto-Continue Attempts
settings.desc: How many times a cut-off reply is automatically nudged to continue before asking you. Loop protection can suppress it.

settings.label: Provider Health
settings.desc: Live status for every provider and server: connected, needs sign-in, unhealthy, or stale — with the reason on each row.

settings.label: Refresh Model List
settings.desc: Re-ask providers what models they offer right now — useful after a provider launches something new.

settings.label: Auto-Update Model List at Startup
settings.desc: Checks for new or retired models each time the app starts, so pickers never show ghosts.

settings.label: Auto-Add Free Models
settings.desc: Automatically pulls in newly free models as they appear. A 'last checked' time shows below; failures flag for attention.

settings.label: Usage Windows Shown
settings.desc: Which time spans the usage view tracks — the classic 5-hour and 7-day windows match most provider limits.

settings.label: Providers on the Usage Board
settings.desc: Pick which providers appear in the quota summary. Hiding one doesn't stop tracking it.

settings.label: Show Quota Reset Timer
settings.desc: Shows 'Resets in 2h 15m' style countdowns so you know when a maxed-out account comes back.

settings.label: Show Account Cooldowns
settings.desc: Displays rest-period timers next to accounts in pickers and the usage widget, so you see who's benched and until when.

settings.label: Show Usage Pressure Warnings
settings.desc: Surfaces little pressure indicators when accounts get close to limits, before anything actually stops.

settings.label: Usage Chart Style
settings.desc: How usage history is drawn — bars, a line, or a filled area. Purely cosmetic.

settings.label: Cost Export Format
settings.desc: File format when exporting your spend ledger — CSV opens in spreadsheets, JSON suits other tools.

settings.label: Cost Rows Per Page
settings.desc: How many entries the spend ledger shows at once.

settings.label: Tool Stats Window
settings.desc: Time span for the tool-usage widget on the Usage page.

settings.label: Monthly Spend Limit (USD)
settings.desc: A dollar ceiling for the month. What happens at the limit is set by the budget policy below. 0 means unlimited.

settings.label: Monthly Token Budget
settings.desc: A token-count ceiling for the month, feeding pressure warnings and run limits. 0 means unlimited.

settings.label: Per-Run Spend Budget
settings.desc: Money or token allowance for a single run, frozen when the run starts so pausing doesn't reset it.

settings.label: When the Budget Runs Out
settings.desc: Block at the limit (safest for your wallet), just warn and keep going, or allow overage. Sources disagreed; blocking wins.

settings.label: Budget Warning Point
settings.desc: Warn when spending or quota use passes this share of a limit, so you can react before anything blocks.

settings.label: Pressure Alert Sensitivity
settings.desc: How jumpy the usage-pressure alerts are. High warns early and often; low waits until things are genuinely tight.

settings.label: Quota & Budget Console
settings.desc: One place to review and adjust every quota and execution-budget control together.

settings.label: Helper Wave Spending Cap
settings.desc: Max spend for one wave of helper agents, so a burst of parallel helpers can't torch the budget.

settings.label: Max Tool Steps Per Agent
settings.desc: Hard cap on back-and-forth tool calls one agent can make, stopping infinite loops before they cost you.

settings.label: Max Time Per Run
settings.desc: Hard time limit for a run (default 20 min), frozen at start and honored across pause/resume. Goals have a separate seconds cap.

settings.label: Max Goal Continuations
settings.desc: How many scheduler rounds an autonomous goal may take before it must stop and check in.

settings.label: Per-Node Time Limit (ms)
settings.desc: Time cap for a single work node inside a helper's envelope. Can tighten the parent's budget, never exceed it.

settings.label: Pressure & Rate-Limit History
settings.desc: Read-only log of past pressure episodes and rate-limit hits per account — useful for spotting a chronically tight account.

settings.label: Keep Usage History For
settings.desc: How long detailed usage records are kept before being archived and compacted.

settings.label: Price Table Version
settings.desc: Which provider price list cost estimates use. Your own overrides apply before any cost warnings fire.

settings.label: Permission Preset
settings.desc: One-click safety level. Read Only can't change anything; Plan can research and propose; Regular asks before risky steps; Full rarely asks.

settings.label: Default Answer for New Tools
settings.desc: What happens when the AI uses a tool with no rule yet: allow it, ask you first, or block it. 'Ask' keeps you in control.

settings.label: Assistant Chat Mode
settings.desc: Regular asks before each action in chat. YOLO skips approval prompts for that chat — file and command guards still apply.

settings.label: Per-Tool Permissions
settings.desc: Set allow/ask/deny for each tool: run commands, edit files, read, search, questions, to-do list, skills, code intel. Reading is safe to allow.

settings.label: Custom Permission Rules
settings.desc: Pattern rules like 'github_*: ask'. Checked top to bottom; the last matching rule wins. Drag to reorder. For fine-grained control.

settings.label: Editing Scope
settings.desc: Choose which layer you are editing rules for: everywhere, this project, or a package, seam, or lane inside it. Narrower layers win.

settings.label: Project & Lane Overrides
settings.desc: Let a project — or a package, seam, or lane inside it — use its own rules instead of inheriting yours. Overrides can only narrow, not widen.

settings.label: Show Where Rules Come From
settings.desc: Adds a small badge next to each permission showing which layer set it (global, project, lane), so surprises are easy to trace.

settings.label: Show Requested vs Granted Powers
settings.desc: When the AI gets less access than it asked for, show exactly what was trimmed and which rule did it. Useful for debugging blocks.

settings.label: Permissions View Style
settings.desc: Simple view shows presets and plain dropdowns only. Expert view adds pattern rules, profiles, and allowlists. Start Simple.

settings.label: Rule Storage Location
settings.desc: Rules are saved as TOML files: one in your app config folder, one per project. Shown for reference; editing by hand is rarely needed.

settings.label: How Independent Is the AI?
settings.desc: Hands-off runs on its own and only interrupts for critical issues. Ask-me-first pauses at every checkpoint you enable below.

settings.label: Pause at Each Seam
settings.desc: The run stops for your OK before crossing each seam — the boundary between major stretches of work. Off means it keeps going.

settings.label: Pause at Each Package
settings.desc: The run stops for your OK before starting the next package of work. Independent of the other pause settings.

settings.label: Pause at Each Lane
settings.desc: The run stops for your OK before each individual lane of work. The most frequent checkpoint — expect many prompts.

settings.label: Always Ask About These
settings.desc: Actions that always need your OK when supervision is on: passwords, billing, deleting things, outside services, security changes.

settings.label: Require a Written Plan First
settings.desc: Make the AI show you a detailed plan before doing the work, at the levels you pick. Slower but much more predictable.

settings.label: Always Ask Before Publishing
settings.desc: Anything that pushes outside your machine — Docker Hub, servers, releases — always needs your OK. YOLO mode cannot skip this.

settings.label: Extra Approval for Risky Actions
settings.desc: Destructive changes, production systems, data deletion, new dependencies, and credentials always get an explicit approval step.

settings.label: Where Approval Requests Appear
settings.desc: Choose where you get pinged when the AI is waiting on you: the dashboard, system tray, assistant chat, or all of them.

settings.label: Preview Commands Before They Run
settings.desc: Shows the exact command, folder, and risk level before a terminal command executes, so you can see what you are approving.

settings.label: Default Approval Choice
settings.desc: When you approve something, how long it stays approved: just this once, for this session, or always. 'Always' creates a lasting rule.

settings.label: Options Shown When Blocked
settings.desc: When an action is blocked, you get context-aware fixes: approve once, approve for session, always allow, or open the matching setting.

settings.label: When You Don't Answer
settings.desc: What happens if an approval request sits unanswered: wait forever, re-ask, or mark it as a long wait so the run can be triaged.

settings.label: Approve & Keep Going
settings.desc: After you approve one gate, the run continues past later gates without pausing again. Faster, but you review less.

settings.label: Resume Instantly After You Answer
settings.desc: The moment you approve or reject, the run wakes up and continues instead of waiting for the next scheduled check.

settings.label: When the AI Repeats Itself
settings.desc: If the AI runs the exact same action over and over, stop and ask you, let it continue, or block it. Catches stuck loops early.

settings.label: Repeats Before Stepping In
settings.desc: How many identical actions in a row before the repeat guard triggers. Lower catches loops sooner but interrupts more.

settings.label: Loop Detection Style
settings.desc: How aggressively runaway patterns are detected: strict stops fastest, bounded allows a set number, adaptive learns per pattern.

settings.label: Stop After Repeated Command Failures
settings.desc: If the same command fails this many times in a row, the run stops instead of burning time and money retrying.

settings.label: Stop When a File Is Rewritten Too Often
settings.desc: If the same file is rewritten more than this many times in 10 minutes, the run is stopped — a classic sign of a stuck loop.

settings.label: Stop After Repeated Provider Errors
settings.desc: How many recoverable AI-provider or executor errors are tolerated before the run gives up and reports back.

settings.label: Debug: Max Parallel Browser Tests
settings.desc: How many browser scenarios the automated debug loop may explore at once while gathering evidence. Higher is faster but heavier.

settings.label: Debug: Stop When Nothing New Is Found
settings.desc: The automated debug loop stops after this many passes that turn up no new evidence, instead of spinning forever.

settings.label: Debug Mode Standing Permissions
settings.desc: What debugging may do repeatedly without re-asking: read evidence and low-risk checks. Risky changes are still asked one by one.

settings.label: Show Debug Permission Status
settings.desc: Inspect whether the debug automation profile is active, degraded, or blocked, including which powers it has and when they expire.

settings.label: Plan Mode Can't Be Escaped
settings.desc: Hard guarantee that a run in plan mode cannot make changes, checked before every action. The AI itself cannot lower this ceiling.

settings.label: Strict Command Approval Matching
settings.desc: An approval covers exactly the command you saw — same wording, folder, and purpose. Prevents one OK being reused for something else.

settings.label: Loosen Defaults Only When You're Around
settings.desc: Tools default to 'allow' only when you are present to be asked; unattended runs fall back to stricter defaults automatically.

settings.label: Show Approval History
settings.desc: Keeps a searchable record of everything you approved or rejected, in-thread and in an audit inspector.

settings.label: Log Blocked Actions
settings.desc: Every denied tool call and declined prompt is written to the audit log, so you can review what the AI tried to do.

settings.label: Keep Honest Records of Skips & Stops
settings.desc: Skipped steps are never shown as successes, and the history of paused or rejected work survives an abort.

settings.label: Write Approval Strictness
settings.desc: How broadly one write approval applies in this project: strict covers the least, permissive the most. Restrictive is a safe middle.

settings.label: Block Dangerous Commands
settings.desc: Stops commands that could wipe files or databases (rm -rf, drop database) before they run. Leave this on.

settings.label: Protect Secret Files
settings.desc: Blocks the AI from touching passwords, .env files, API keys, and SSH keys. Turning this off exposes your credentials.

settings.label: Keep Writes Inside the Plan
settings.desc: The AI may only change files that the current piece of work declared it would touch. Prevents surprise edits elsewhere.

settings.label: Web Access Permissions
settings.desc: Control each web ability separately: search, read pages via Site Reader, extract, research, crawl, and map sites. 'Ask' is safest.

settings.label: Strict Write Checking
settings.desc: Applies the tightest interpretation of allowed write areas. Turn off only if legitimate edits keep getting blocked.

settings.label: Allow Dangerous Commands (Override)
settings.desc: Master override that lets rm, dd, and similar commands through the blocklist. Requires explicit confirmation. Keep off.

settings.label: Trusted Commands List
settings.desc: Commands you have personally exempted from the blocklist, usually added via 'Approve & add to list' in chat. Review occasionally.

settings.label: Extra Blocked Patterns File
settings.desc: A project file listing additional command patterns to block, on top of the built-in list. Additive only — it can't unblock anything.

settings.label: Folders Outside the Project
settings.desc: Folders beyond your project the AI may touch without asking. Supports wildcards and ~. Everything else triggers the guard below.

settings.label: Outside-Folder Guard
settings.desc: What happens when the AI reaches for a path outside your project roots: allow, ask you, or block. Allowlisted folders skip this.

settings.label: Relax Guards During Interviews
settings.desc: Lets the AI read normally protected files while interviewing you about the project. Safer to keep off and approve case by case.

settings.label: Allow Resets During Testing
settings.desc: Lets verification steps run otherwise-blocked commands like test-database resets. Only applies inside the checking gate.

settings.label: Allow Secret Access During Audits
settings.desc: Lets the security-audit check read protected files so it can actually inspect them. Applies only during that verification step.

settings.label: Protected Paths Need Sign-Off
settings.desc: Marks certain paths as protected so changing them requires a governance-level approval, not just a normal OK.

settings.label: Catch Overlapping Edits
settings.desc: Detects when two parallel workers plan to edit the same files and forces them to take turns or work in isolation.

settings.label: Roll Back When You Reject
settings.desc: When you reject a change, work restarts from the last known-good restore point instead of on top of the bad attempt.

settings.label: Hide Sensitive Data in Output
settings.desc: A profile of patterns (keys, emails, tokens) scrubbed from logs and displays before anything is shown or saved.

settings.label: Blur Secrets in Screenshots
settings.desc: Applies a redaction profile to captured screenshots so on-screen secrets never end up stored in run history.

settings.label: File Protection System
settings.desc: The engine behind all file and command guards. Fail-closed: if it can't start, risky actions are blocked rather than allowed.

settings.label: Terminal Colors
settings.desc: Color scheme for the built-in terminal, separate from the app theme. Includes text, cursor, selection, and status colors.

settings.label: Terminal Font
settings.desc: Typeface used in terminal panes. Custom fonts load from your fonts folder; changing family needs an app restart.

settings.label: Terminal Text Size
settings.desc: How big terminal text appears, in pixels. You can also zoom in and out with keyboard shortcuts.

settings.label: Shell
settings.desc: Which command-line program runs inside new terminal panes. Leave on system default unless you know you want another.

settings.label: Starting Folder
settings.desc: Folder new terminals open in. Project root keeps commands running where your code lives; some docs preferred your home folder.

settings.label: Copy When I Highlight
settings.desc: Automatically copies any text you select in the terminal, so you can paste without pressing copy. Off avoids surprise clipboard changes.

settings.label: Right-Click to Paste
settings.desc: Pastes your clipboard when you right-click in the terminal, like classic terminal apps.

settings.label: Before Closing a Busy Terminal
settings.desc: What happens when you close a terminal that is still running something. Asking first prevents accidentally stopping builds or servers.

settings.label: Explain What Commands Do
settings.desc: Shows plain-English explanations next to commands and terminal states, so you can follow along without knowing the syntax.

settings.label: Reading Aids
settings.desc: Adds line numbers, highlights, and visual cues to terminal output so long logs are easier to scan.

settings.label: Search in Terminal
settings.desc: Lets you search old terminal output (Ctrl+F), tuned to stay fast even on very long transcripts.

settings.label: Preferred Layout
settings.desc: How terminal tabs and panes arrange themselves by default, including the four-pane quadrant workspace.

settings.label: When Reopening a Project
settings.desc: Whether terminals come back exactly how you left them, or you start with a clean slate each time.

settings.label: Keep Terminal History For
settings.desc: How long past terminal output is saved. Longer history helps debugging but uses more disk; docs disagreed, so session-only is kept.

settings.label: Scrollback Lines
settings.desc: Maximum lines of output kept in memory per terminal. Lower numbers use less memory on chatty commands.

settings.label: Copy & Paste Style
settings.desc: Whether copied terminal text keeps its exact spacing or gets tidied up, plus how selection pasting behaves.

settings.label: Terminal Shortcuts
settings.desc: Remap terminal-only keys like search, next match, scrollback jump, font size, and clear — separate from app-wide shortcuts.

settings.label: Run When a Terminal Opens
settings.desc: A command that runs automatically in every new terminal, like loading your shell profile or environment.

settings.label: Allowed Shell Profiles
settings.desc: Which shell and environment setups this project may offer when opening terminals. Session overrides stay narrow.

settings.label: Terminal Look & Feel Preset
settings.desc: How rich the terminal surface looks. The effective preset is disclosed when it differs from what you asked for.

settings.label: Keep Command Titles Visible
settings.desc: Pins each command's header while you scroll its output, so you always know which command produced what.

settings.label: Performance Mode
settings.desc: Reduces visual polish to keep the terminal fast during very heavy output. Docs disagreed on the default; off keeps full fidelity.

settings.label: Shell Integration Status
settings.desc: Shows whether Puppet Master's smart shell features (command blocks, cwd tracking) are active in your shell.

settings.label: Font Rendering
settings.desc: Fine-tunes how terminal text is drawn. Try Crisp if text looks blurry on your display.

settings.label: Tab Purpose Hints
settings.desc: Optional label for what a terminal tab is for (build, server, logs). Purely organizational; never changes what runs.

settings.label: Auto-Open a Second Pane
settings.desc: Opens a second terminal section automatically. Off by default — extra panes appear only when you ask or a policy explains why.

settings.label: Terminal Debug Logging
settings.desc: Records extra technical detail about terminal sessions for troubleshooting. Leave off unless support asks for it.

settings.label: Wrap Long Lines
settings.desc: Folds long lines so you never scroll sideways. Off is the norm for code; on is comfier for prose.

settings.label: Line Numbers
settings.desc: Shows a number next to every line so chat, diffs, and error messages can point you to the exact spot.

settings.label: Color-Code My Files
settings.desc: Colors code by meaning so files are easier to read. Gets smarter automatically when a language server is running.

settings.label: Language Smarts
settings.desc: Turns on language servers: error checking, hover explanations, autocomplete, and jump-to-definition while you browse code.

settings.label: Problem Highlighting
settings.desc: Which code problems get flagged in the editor and problems panel. Docs disagreed on the control style; this level picker is kept.

settings.label: Auto-Tidy Code
settings.desc: Runs code formatters to keep files neatly styled. Turning this off skips every formatter, built-in and custom.

settings.label: Start With Editor Strip Collapsed
settings.desc: Remembers per project whether the in-app editor strip starts folded away or open.

settings.label: Jump Highlight Duration (ms)
settings.desc: How long a line stays highlighted after you jump to it from chat or a diff, so your eye can find it.

settings.label: Big File Preview Limit (Lines)
settings.desc: Files longer than this open in a truncated preview with a Load Full button, keeping the app snappy.

settings.label: Never Open Files Bigger Than (MB)
settings.desc: Hard safety cap — files above this size show a 'too large' notice instead of loading and freezing the app.

settings.label: Formatter Catalog
settings.desc: Per-language formatter list (21 built in): turn each on or off, change its command, environment, and which file types it handles.

settings.label: Add a Custom Formatter
settings.desc: Register your own formatter with a name, command, and file types. Custom ones can be removed; built-ins can only be disabled or reset.

settings.label: Language Server Catalog
settings.desc: Per-language server list: enable or disable each, and override its launch command, file types, environment, and startup options.

settings.label: Add a Custom Language Server
settings.desc: Register your own language server with a unique name, command, and file types. Edit, remove, or reset catalog entries here too.

settings.label: Project Root Override
settings.desc: Tell language servers where your project really starts when auto-detection guesses wrong (common in unusual folder layouts).

settings.label: Server Attachment Info
settings.desc: Shows which language server is attached to which folder, including remote setups. Mostly read-only until servers report identity.

settings.label: Restart Crashed Servers
settings.desc: Automatically brings a language server back if it crashes, so error checking quietly keeps working.

settings.label: Restart Language Servers Now
settings.desc: Manually restarts language servers — the classic fix when highlighting or errors get stuck. Also restarts after settings changes.

settings.label: Hover Tip Delay (ms)
settings.desc: How long your cursor rests on code before an explanation tooltip appears. Higher feels calmer; lower feels snappier.

settings.label: Hover Tip Timeout (ms)
settings.desc: How long to wait for a hover explanation before giving up. Late answers are discarded so stale info never shows.

settings.label: Autocomplete Timeout (ms)
settings.desc: How long to wait for autocomplete suggestions before showing what's already available.

settings.label: Symbol Search Timeout (ms)
settings.desc: How long project-wide symbol searches may run before stopping. Big projects may need more time.

settings.label: Typing Sync Delay (ms)
settings.desc: How long after you stop typing before edits are sent to language servers. Batches keystrokes to save work.

settings.label: Server Memory Limit (MB)
settings.desc: Maximum memory each language server may use before being reined in. Protects the rest of your machine.

settings.label: Server CPU Limit per Request (s)
settings.desc: Maximum processing time a single language-server request may take before it's cancelled.

settings.label: Prefer Language Experts for Fixes
settings.desc: When picking a helper agent for a code problem, lean toward one that knows that language, using live error info as the hint.

settings.label: How Much Freedom Agents Get
settings.desc: Ask and Plan only look, never touch. Regular checks with you before big actions. YOLO runs fully hands-off with safety guardrails.

settings.label: Publishing Images
settings.desc: Whether finished container builds upload automatically or wait for you. Manual keeps you in control of what goes public.

settings.label: Show Docker Tools Only When Needed
settings.desc: Hides the Docker Manager panel in projects with no containers, keeping the workspace clean. It appears when a Dockerfile shows up.

settings.label: Docker Hub Sign-In Method
settings.desc: How Puppet Master proves who you are to Docker Hub: a pasted access token or a browser sign-in.

settings.label: Docker Hub Access Token
settings.desc: Your Docker Hub token, stored safely in the system keychain — never in app files. Needed before publishing images.

settings.label: Connect Docker Hub
settings.desc: Sign in via browser, test that saved credentials still work, or clear them. Refreshes what your account is allowed to do.

settings.label: Docker Hub Namespace
settings.desc: Which Docker Hub account or team your images publish under. Lists what your sign-in can access.

settings.label: Docker Hub Repository
settings.desc: The specific repository your images publish to, with a refresh button to re-list what's available.

settings.label: Create a New Repository
settings.desc: Makes a fresh Docker Hub repository from inside the app — separate from the confirmation you see when publishing.

settings.label: New Repositories Are
settings.desc: Whether repositories you create start out visible to everyone or private to you.

settings.label: Default Image Registry
settings.desc: Where container images are pulled from and pushed to when you don't say otherwise.

settings.label: Who Runs the Tools
settings.desc: Hosted keeps Puppet Master executing every tool itself (recommended); Delegated lets the agent run its own. Docs disagreed on wording.

settings.label: Force Delegated Execution
settings.desc: Advanced override for CLI-bridged runs: with provider approval it switches Regular mode to delegated execution. No effect elsewhere.

settings.label: Workflow Overlay
settings.desc: Optional working style layered on a run — Debug, Interview, or Brainstorm. Never grants more power than the run mode allows.

settings.label: Container Engine
settings.desc: Which container engine Puppet Master talks to on this machine.

settings.label: Docker Program Location
settings.desc: Point to the docker program if it isn't found automatically (unusual installs only).

settings.label: Default Docker/Kubernetes View
settings.desc: Which context the Docker Manager shows first when you open it.

settings.label: Other Registry Sign-Ins
settings.desc: Credentials for registries besides Docker Hub. Kept separate from your AI provider accounts.

settings.label: Company Registry Rules
settings.desc: Per-host registry policies for work setups: trust, proxy, certificates, allowed actions, and the default push target.

settings.label: Image Tag Templates
settings.desc: Patterns for naming published images automatically, using {version}, {timestamp}, or {commit}.

settings.label: Show Older Publishes in Chain View
settings.desc: Includes past publishes in the version chain, not just the latest run.

settings.label: Follow Newest Publish
settings.desc: Keeps views pointed at your most recent publish automatically.

settings.label: Compose File Location
settings.desc: Where your docker-compose file lives if it isn't in the usual spot.

settings.label: Compose Project Naming
settings.desc: How compose stacks get their names — automatic from the folder, or a name you pick.

settings.label: Build Context Folder
settings.desc: The folder sent to Docker when building images. Usually the project root.

settings.label: Dockerfile Location
settings.desc: Where the Dockerfile lives if it isn't at the project root.

settings.label: Build Stage
settings.desc: For multi-stage Dockerfiles: which stage to build (e.g. just 'dev' instead of everything).

settings.label: Build For These Chips
settings.desc: Which processor types your images support (e.g. Apple Silicon and Intel). Shows whether multi-platform builds are ready.

settings.label: Show Advanced Build Options
settings.desc: Reveals extra build arguments in the Docker Manager's Build view.

settings.label: Open Containers In
settings.desc: Which browser opens your running app. A choice is required — there's no longer a silent fallback to the system default.

settings.label: Port Guessing Order
settings.desc: When opening a container's web page, which ports to try first. Reorder if your app always lives on an unusual port.

settings.label: Shell Inside Containers
settings.desc: Command used when you open a terminal inside a running container (e.g. bash or sh).

settings.label: When a Port Opens
settings.desc: Whether forwarded ports open in your browser automatically, just get suggested, or stay quiet.

settings.label: Log Streams Start
settings.desc: Whether live logs scroll along automatically or start paused. Each stream remembers your choice.

settings.label: Config Drift Alerts
settings.desc: How eagerly to warn when running containers no longer match their config files.

settings.label: Ignore These in Drift Checks
settings.desc: Files and labels drift detection should skip, so expected differences stop triggering warnings.

settings.label: Compare Drift Against
settings.desc: What running containers are compared to when checking for drift.

settings.label: Operation Receipts
settings.desc: How much detail is kept about each container operation you run.

settings.label: Keep Receipts For
settings.desc: How long records of container operations stick around.

settings.label: Disk Cleanup Style
settings.desc: How boldly the Cleanup Advisor suggests deleting old images, containers, and volumes. Conservative never surprises you.

settings.label: Cleanup Scan Schedule
settings.desc: How often disk usage is scanned for cleanup suggestions.

settings.label: Warn at Disk Usage (%)
settings.desc: Shows a warning when Docker's disk usage passes this percentage.

settings.label: Skip Warnings for Throwaway Previews
settings.desc: Silences cleanup warnings for short-lived preview containers that clean themselves up anyway.

settings.label: Never Clean These Up
settings.desc: Images, containers, or labels the cleanup tools must always leave alone.

settings.label: Kubernetes Cluster
settings.desc: Which Kubernetes cluster (kubeconfig context) this project talks to. Separate from your AI provider identity.

settings.label: Kubernetes Namespace
settings.desc: Which slice of the cluster this project works in.

settings.label: Show Whole-Cluster Resources
settings.desc: Shows everything on the cluster instead of just this project's resources. Off keeps things focused.

settings.label: Live-Update Kubernetes Views
settings.desc: Keeps Kubernetes panels refreshing automatically as things change.

settings.label: Kubernetes Log Defaults
settings.desc: Default follow/paused/historical behavior for the Kubernetes log viewer.

settings.label: Show Helm Tools
settings.desc: Shows Helm chart tooling when Helm files are detected in the project.

settings.label: Kubernetes Safety Policy
settings.desc: Which clusters, namespaces, and actions (apply, exec, port-forward, logs) agents are ever allowed to touch.

settings.label: Remote Machines (SSH)
settings.desc: Saved remote computers: nickname, address, user, and auth method. Passwords and keys stay in the system keychain, never app files.

settings.label: Debug Setups
settings.desc: Saved run-and-debug launch profiles for stepping through your app with the standard debug protocol; profile fields per the launch profile schema (FinalGUISpec F3-489).

settings.label: Update Unraid Template After Publish
settings.desc: After each image publish, regenerates the Unraid app template so your server listing stays current.

settings.label: Auto-Manage the Template Repo
settings.desc: Hands the Unraid template repository's housekeeping (layout, commits) to Puppet Master.

settings.label: Set Up Template Repository
settings.desc: Create a new Unraid template repo or connect an existing one; checks the branch and layout, and offers one-click push.

settings.label: Review Template Repo Health
settings.desc: Appears when the template repo looks off — bad config, diverged from remote, or unrelated changes — and walks you through fixing it.

settings.label: Template Repo Location
settings.desc: Where the Unraid template repository lives — a local folder or a Git remote URL.

settings.label: Template Repo Branch
settings.desc: Which branch template updates are committed to.

settings.label: Template Repo Name
settings.desc: Name for the template repository; the default is built from your project name.

settings.label: Maintainer Folder Override
settings.desc: Custom folder name inside the template repo, if you don't want your Docker Hub namespace used.

settings.label: Auto-Push Template Updates
settings.desc: Pushes template commits to the remote automatically. Off means you review and push with one click instead.

settings.label: Your Publisher Name
settings.desc: The name shown to people who install your app from Unraid Community Apps. Required before auto-publishing.

settings.label: About You
settings.desc: A short blurb about you or your team, shown on your publisher page. Required before auto-publishing.

settings.label: Support Link
settings.desc: Where users go for help with your apps — a forum thread, Discord, or GitHub issues. Required before auto-publishing.

settings.label: Publisher Icon
settings.desc: Your publisher picture: upload an image (copied into the managed repo) or link to one by URL. Required before auto-publishing.

settings.label: Publisher Profile Applies
settings.desc: Use one shared publisher profile everywhere, or override it per project.

settings.label: Publisher Handle
settings.desc: Short machine-friendly name for your publisher profile; defaults to your Docker Hub namespace.

settings.label: Edit Publisher Profile File
settings.desc: Open the underlying profile file (ca_profile.xml) in a friendly form, or as raw XML for fields the form doesn't cover.

settings.label: Keep Unrecognized Profile Content
settings.desc: When saving the publisher profile, preserves any hand-added XML the app doesn't understand instead of deleting it.

settings.label: App Listing Name
settings.desc: The name your app shows in the Unraid store. Falls back to the project name; required before auto-publishing.

settings.label: App Web Address
settings.desc: The URL pattern for opening your app's interface, usually detected from previews automatically.

settings.label: App Description
settings.desc: What your app does, shown in the store listing. Starts from your README; required before auto-publishing.

settings.label: App Store Categories
settings.desc: Which store categories your app appears under. Required before auto-publishing.

settings.label: App Setup Fields
settings.desc: The ports, folders, and options users fill in when installing your app — detected from compose or edited by hand.

settings.label: App-Wide Rules
settings.desc: Standing instructions given to every agent run in every project. Seeded from your AGENTS.md the first time you launch.
settings.default: Seeded from AGENTS.md on first run

settings.label: Project Rules
settings.desc: Extra instructions that apply only to this project. Stored in .puppet-master/project-rules.md so they travel with the repo.

settings.label: Show Instructions In Runs
settings.desc: How much of the assembled instructions (rules, policy packs, persona) you see alongside each run: nothing, a summary, or everything.

settings.label: Which Rule Packs To List
settings.desc: Filters the rule-pack list to only active packs, everything, or everything except disabled ones. Also flags packs with load errors.

settings.label: Reuse-First Guard
settings.desc: Nudges agents to reuse existing code before writing new code. Turning it off never bypasses safety, secrets, or permission rules.

settings.label: Instruction Packing Style
settings.desc: Whether AGENTS.md and rules go in whole, trimmed to a size cap, or as short excerpts. Trimming saves tokens but may drop detail.

settings.label: Memory Notes Size Cap
settings.desc: Hard cap in tokens on remembered notes injected before each assistant message. Bigger caps mean more recall but pricier turns.

settings.label: Max Memories Per Turn
settings.desc: How many remembered notes can be added to a single turn (verified notes only, summaries only). Fewer keeps prompts lean.

settings.label: Show What Got Packed In
settings.desc: Lists every file and note injected into a run with its size, so you can see exactly what the AI was given.

settings.label: Show Final Prompt Preview
settings.desc: Lets you peek at the fully assembled prompt (system prompt, persona, rules, journal) before it's sent. Handy for debugging odd behavior.

settings.label: Track Instruction Sources
settings.desc: Records where each instruction came from (path, hash, precedence) and why any were denied, so mystery behavior is traceable.

settings.label: Block Instruction Loops
settings.desc: Stops instruction files that import each other in a circle from bloating or breaking the prompt. Leave on unless debugging.

settings.label: Quarantine Broken Turns
settings.desc: Checks each model or tool reply for corruption before saving it to history, so one malformed turn can't poison later runs.

settings.label: Keep Changing Bits Separate
settings.desc: Keeps date, folder, and git status out of the cacheable prompt base so caching keeps working and costs stay down.

settings.label: Explain Cache Effects
settings.desc: Shows how each change affects prompt caching and cost, including when a manual context squeeze resets the cache.

settings.label: Skip Duplicate Content
settings.desc: Stores identical files or results once and references them, instead of packing the same bytes into context repeatedly.

settings.label: Stable Prompt Baseline
settings.desc: Keeps the prompt's base fingerprint steady when only volatile details change, so caching and comparisons stay reliable.

settings.label: Remember Between Sessions
settings.desc: Lets the assistant keep useful notes across conversations and projects. Turn off for a clean slate every time.

settings.label: How Much History To Keep
settings.desc: How much past conversation the assistant holds onto for this project — nothing, just recent, everything, or a custom window.

settings.label: How Memories Are Found
settings.desc: Picks memories by meaning, by how recent they are, or a blend of both. Hybrid works best for most people.

settings.label: When Memories Are Pulled In
settings.desc: Automatic pulls relevant memories in for you; manual waits for you to ask; hybrid does both. Automatic is the easy default.

settings.label: Restore Context On Start
settings.desc: How the assistant reloads what it knew when a session starts: right away, only when needed, only when you ask, or never.

settings.label: Keyword vs Meaning Balance
settings.desc: Slides memory search between exact-word matching and meaning-based matching. The two weights always add up to 1.

settings.label: How Fast Memories Fade
settings.desc: Fade time in days for each kind of memory (current work 14, blockers 21, constraints 180, and more). Editable per note.

settings.label: Fade Finished Work Faster
settings.desc: Memories about finished work fade at this fraction of their normal lifespan, so stale notes stop crowding out fresh ones.

settings.label: Save Unconfirmed Notes
settings.desc: Keeps notes the AI proposed but hasn't verified yet at the end of a run. Off means only confirmed facts survive.

settings.label: Trust Manual Confirms
settings.desc: Lets you mark a memory as verified without the app re-checking it. Off keeps the automatic double-check — the safer choice.

settings.label: Use Pinned Unconfirmed Notes
settings.desc: Allows pinned but unverified memories into prompts. Off keeps runs on confirmed facts only, which avoids compounding mistakes.

settings.label: Memory Review Starting View
settings.desc: Which memories the review panel shows first when opened. Starting on unconfirmed notes keeps your attention where it matters.

settings.label: Helpers Can Read Memory
settings.desc: Lets helper agents see the main assistant's memories. Off keeps each helper's head empty of your history — the private default.

settings.label: Memory Cleanup Tools
settings.desc: One-click chores: rebuild search indexes, sweep for duplicates, re-verify notes, compress old months, or prune and archive.

settings.label: Per-Run Token Budget
settings.desc: Caps how many tokens one run may spend before stopping for your OK. Separate from any monthly spending budget.

settings.label: Per-Goal Token Budget
settings.desc: A hard token ceiling across every run working toward one goal. Runs that hit it stop with a budget-limited status.

settings.label: Max Context Size (kTokens)
settings.desc: How big each run's working memory can grow. The app clamps this to what your chosen model actually supports.

settings.label: Memory Lookup Window
settings.desc: How far back memory searches reach. Extended finds more but burns more tokens each turn.

settings.label: Auto-Shrink Old Context
settings.desc: Quietly summarizes stale context when space runs low so long runs keep going instead of hitting the ceiling.

settings.label: Context Squeeze Mode
settings.desc: Automatic squeezes context at pressure thresholds; manual waits for you; disabled lets runs fail when full.

settings.label: Squeeze Context Now
settings.desc: Compacts the current session's context on demand and shows usage, tokens, and cost before/after.

settings.label: Max Squeezes In A Row
settings.desc: Stops context squeezing from repeating endlessly in one run. One pass is almost always enough.

settings.label: Start Warning At (% Full)
settings.desc: When context reaches this percent full, the app starts warning and gently trimming. Lower means earlier, gentler trims.

settings.label: Squeeze Hard At (% Full)
settings.desc: Past this percent full, the app compacts aggressively to avoid a mid-run failure.

settings.label: Low Headroom Alert (%)
settings.desc: Warns you when remaining context drops below this percent, so you can wrap up or squeeze before the run stalls.

settings.label: Big Chunk Cutoff (Tokens)
settings.desc: Anything larger than this counts as a big chunk and gets trimmed first when space runs out.

settings.label: Protected Context Share (%)
settings.desc: Percent of context reserved for must-keep content that squeezing never touches. Overridable per model.

settings.label: Context Space Split
settings.desc: How context space is divided between protected content, history, the current turn, tool results, and spare. Must total 100.

settings.label: Tool Output In Context
settings.desc: Whether tool results go into context whole, summarized, as headers only, or not at all. Trimming saves space, loses detail.

settings.label: Cap Local Model Context
settings.desc: Keeps helper, memory, and side-agent models on small-model-sized context so nothing quietly stuffs in full history.

settings.label: Interview Style
settings.desc: Guided walks you through set steps; freeform lets you talk naturally; hybrid adapts. Guided is safest if you're new.

settings.label: Interview Output Format
settings.desc: File format for the requirements document the interview produces. Markdown is easiest to read and share.

settings.label: Question Style
settings.desc: How the Planning Wizard phrases its questions: structured checklists, casual conversation, or as few words as possible.

settings.label: Suggest The Planning Wizard
settings.desc: When you describe a big feature in chat, the app offers to open the Planning Wizard so nothing gets missed.

settings.label: Open Wizard After First Setup
settings.desc: After you finish connecting providers for the first time, land in the Planning Wizard instead of an empty screen.

settings.label: Allow Skipping Provider Setup
settings.desc: Lets you press 'Skip for now' during setup and try the Planning Wizard in a limited state before connecting anything.

settings.label: Open Finished Plans For Review
settings.desc: When a Deep Plan finishes, it opens in the editor so you can read and annotate it before anything runs.

settings.label: Keep Plan Panel Pinned
settings.desc: Keeps the plan visible in the sidebar while work runs, so you always see what step the app is on.

settings.label: Wizard Starting Point
settings.desc: Tell the wizard what kind of project this is — brand new, forking an existing app, improving one, or contributing a change.

settings.label: Project Folder
settings.desc: Where the wizard creates your new project, or the existing folder it should work in.

settings.label: Requirements Upload Limit
settings.desc: Most files you can attach as requirements for one plan (hard cap 10). Keeps the wizard focused on what matters.

settings.label: Max Size Per Requirements File
settings.desc: Largest single file (in bytes) you can attach as a requirement — 5 MB by default. Oversized files are rejected before saving.

settings.label: Reorder Requirements Files
settings.desc: Drag your attached files into priority order — earlier files win when documents disagree.

settings.label: Plan Thoroughness
settings.desc: How deep planning digs: fewer questions and a lighter plan, or more research and detail. Comprehensive costs more time.

settings.label: Web Research During Planning
settings.desc: Whether planning may look things up on the web via Site Reader. 'Ask' checks with you first each time.

settings.label: Auto Checklist For Big Tasks
settings.desc: For multi-step work outside planning modes, the app builds its own checklist so steps don't get dropped.

settings.label: Interview Topics Included
settings.desc: Which topics the interview covers. Skipping topics speeds things up but leaves gaps the app will guess at.

settings.label: Interview & Builder Preferences
settings.desc: Fine-grained overrides for the interview, requirements builder, and wizard workflows — most people never need these.

settings.label: Prefer Gemini For Visual Interviews
settings.desc: When Gemini Direct is connected, use it for interview stages that involve screens or images — it's strong at visuals.

settings.label: Opening Scope Questions
settings.desc: How many quick questions the wizard asks up front (1-10) to size your project before choosing which topics to cover.

settings.label: Interview Depth Per Topic
settings.desc: Full asks everything; short caps each topic at 2 questions with no research; skip drops the topic entirely.

settings.label: Question Cap Per Topic
settings.desc: Most questions per interview topic before it wraps up (one grace question allowed). Sources disagreed 1-20 vs preset list; 8 kept.

settings.label: Minimum Questions Per Topic
settings.desc: Fewest questions a topic must ask before it can finish — stops the interview from rushing. Must stay below the cap.

settings.label: Force Full Interview
settings.desc: One-time override: ignore the smart topic picker and run every interview topic at full depth for this session.

settings.label: Hand-Pick Interview Topics
settings.desc: Manually check which topics to run this session — unchecked topics are skipped no matter what the wizard thinks.

settings.label: Confirm Tech Choices With Me
settings.desc: Adds a checkpoint where you explicitly approve the technology stack before the interview moves on.

settings.label: Image Understanding Provider
settings.desc: Which AI handles screenshots and diagrams during interviews. Auto picks whatever connected provider does it best.

settings.label: Builder Helper Selection
settings.desc: How the requirements builder picks its helper personalities: you choose, it chooses, or a mix.

settings.label: Intake Helper
settings.desc: The personality used for the first clarifying-questions stage of the requirements builder.

settings.label: Drafting Helper
settings.desc: The personality that writes the requirements document; falls back to a general-purpose writer if unset.

settings.label: Document Review Lineup
settings.desc: Assign which reviewer personalities check the requirements document on each review round; blanks use sensible fallbacks.

settings.label: Automated Testing
settings.desc: Auto lets the app find and set up tests itself; On requires tests to run; Off forbids them (nothing quietly passes untested).

settings.label: Show Tests While They Run
settings.desc: Watch tests happen in a live window when possible, or let them run quietly in the background with logs only.

settings.label: Built-In Browser Testing
settings.desc: Use the app's own browser to click through your web app and check it works.

settings.label: Visible Browser Automation
settings.desc: Show browser test sessions on screen — navigation, clicks, form fills — so you can watch checks happen.

settings.label: Screenshot Comparison
settings.desc: Take screenshots and compare them against earlier ones to catch visual glitches.

settings.label: Find Testing Tools Online
settings.desc: Let the app research official sources to pick the right testing tools. One source modeled this as a plain on/off toggle.

settings.label: Install Test Tools Automatically
settings.desc: Allow the app to install test frameworks, browsers, and simulators itself, within the permissions you've granted.
