settings.label: Windowed Browser Sessions
settings.desc: Run tests in a normal visible browser window rather than an invisible one.

settings.label: Hot Reload During Tests
settings.desc: Refresh your app instantly as code changes so tests always see the latest version.

settings.label: Live Preview Testing
settings.desc: Use live preview windows to test desktop and native app screens as they update.

settings.label: Desktop App Testing
settings.desc: Automate clicks and typing in desktop application windows to verify they behave.

settings.label: Phone Simulator Testing
settings.desc: Test mobile builds on simulators and emulators instead of real phones.

settings.label: Real Device Testing
settings.desc: Run tests on a physical phone or tablet you've plugged in. Off by default — it needs hardware connected.

settings.label: Accessibility Checks
settings.desc: Verify your app works with screen readers and meets accessibility basics.

settings.label: API Checks
settings.desc: Test that your app's backend endpoints accept and return what they promise.

settings.label: Database Checks
settings.desc: Verify data is actually saved and updated correctly behind the scenes.

settings.label: Console & Network Watching
settings.desc: Capture browser console errors and network traffic during tests to catch hidden failures.

settings.label: Speed & Load Testing
settings.desc: Measure how fast your app responds and whether it holds up under heavy use.

settings.label: Security Testing
settings.desc: Scan for common vulnerabilities and unsafe patterns before they ship.

settings.label: Test Session Controls
settings.desc: Open, watch, collapse, detach, or background a running test session, and inspect its evidence and redactions.

settings.label: GitHub Actions Starter Workflow
settings.desc: Generate a ready-made GitHub test workflow file for your repo. Off by default so nothing is written without you; one source enabled it.

settings.label: Double-Check Finished Work
settings.desc: Runs an independent check on completed work before it counts as done. Turning this off means mistakes slip through faster.

settings.label: When To Show Check Reports
settings.desc: Show verification reports every time, only when something fails, or never. Sources also offered a summary/detailed split.

settings.label: Quality vs Speed
settings.desc: One dial for how picky checks and progress gates are. Thorough catches more but takes longer; fast trusts more.

settings.label: Explain Roadblocks Fully
settings.desc: Blocked work shows the cause, what's affected, the last recovery attempt, and the next safe action — not just 'stuck'.

settings.label: Goal Type
settings.desc: Pick what kind of job this goal is — bug fix, feature build, test-until-pass, and so on. Each type has its own finish line.

settings.label: Progress Pulse (Seconds)
settings.desc: How often running helpers report a heartbeat. Shorter catches stalls sooner; longer is quieter.

settings.label: Detect Stuck Helpers
settings.desc: Notices when a helper stops making progress and flags it for your attention without killing its session.

settings.label: Show Cloud/Local Handoffs
settings.desc: When work moves between cloud and your machine, display what changed — permissions, caches, and tool versions.

settings.label: Verification Strictness
settings.desc: How demanding the final review is, from lenient up to certification-grade proof that everything works.

settings.label: Reviewer Never Grades Own Work
settings.desc: The AI that checks work is always different from the AI that did it — like a second pair of eyes.

settings.label: Auditor Loop
settings.desc: The Auditor re-inspects work with fresh read-only specialists, files findings, repairs, and re-audits until everything is closed.

settings.label: Fix-It Attempts
settings.desc: How the Auditor retries after a failed check: give up immediately, try a limited number of fixes, or keep trying forever.

settings.label: Fix-It Playbook
settings.desc: The order of tactics tried after a failed check — patch, replan, split work, widen context, roll back, and more.

settings.label: When Fixes Run Out
settings.desc: If repair attempts are used up: stop the work entirely, or finish marked 'degraded' so you know it wasn't fully verified.

settings.label: When Checks Can't Run
settings.desc: If the checking system itself is down: fail the work, continue anyway, or pause for your review. Review is safest.

settings.label: Proof Level By Risk
settings.desc: How much proof completion needs: lightweight for read-only work, standard for code, strong for anything destructive. Set per goal risk.

settings.label: Completion Receipts
settings.desc: Every finished piece of work gets a receipt recording what was done and how it was verified — your paper trail.

settings.label: Receipt Strength
settings.desc: What grade of receipt a goal earns — strong ones require replayable evidence plus an independent verifier sign-off.

settings.label: How Much Proof To Capture
settings.desc: How much surrounding context each piece of evidence must include — a single point, its section, or the full document.

settings.label: Keep Evidence Layers Separate
settings.desc: Receipts keep source, process, test, and version-control evidence as separate truth layers so nothing can be blurred together.

settings.label: Enforce Progress Gates
settings.desc: Failed checks can never hide behind a 'done' label — work is blocked until validators actually pass.

settings.label: Require Parallel Review Stages
settings.desc: Refuses to certify work when a required broad parallel review stage was skipped.

settings.label: Checks By Work Type
settings.desc: Assign different validators to different kinds of work nodes — seams, packages, and lanes can each get their own checks.

settings.label: Permissions For Background Goals
settings.desc: Pre-declares what invisible internal goals are allowed to touch; anything out of scope is blocked automatically.

settings.label: Code Health Gate
settings.desc: Uses your editor's live error checking (LSP) as an extra gate — work can't advance while the code shows problems.

settings.label: Code Health Gate Coverage
settings.desc: Check only the files that changed, all open files, or the whole project. Changed files is fastest.

settings.label: What Blocks The Gate
settings.desc: Block on errors only, or on warnings too. Including warnings is stricter but can stall on harmless nags.

settings.label: Where The Gate Applies
settings.desc: Which work boundaries trigger the code health check — at seam, package, or node handoffs. At least one must stay on.

settings.label: Code Check Time Limit
settings.desc: Seconds (5-60) to wait for the code health check before moving on — keeps a slow language server from stalling work.

settings.label: If Code Checking Is Offline
settings.desc: When the language server isn't available: skip the gate quietly, or fail so you know the check never happened.

settings.label: Pick Up Where It Left Off
settings.desc: After a crash or restart, long-running goals resume from their last checkpoint instead of starting over.

settings.label: How Often To Save Progress
settings.desc: How frequently goal mode snapshots its progress. More checkpoints mean safer recovery but slightly slower runs.

settings.label: When To Rethink The Plan
settings.desc: When goal mode builds a fresh plan: only after failures, when work drifts off course, or after every step.

settings.label: When You Change Your Mind Mid-Run
settings.desc: If you make a material change mid-goal: pause and replan, apply it as an immediate hard rule, or just take note.

settings.label: If You Interrupt A Goal
settings.desc: What happens when you step in mid-run: pause the work, cancel it, or ask you which one you meant.

settings.label: Clean Stops
settings.desc: Stopping a run shuts down tools and helpers safely and keeps history intact — a stop is never rewritten as a pass or fail.

settings.label: Flag Real Roadblocks Fast
settings.desc: When the app hits something it truly cannot solve, it tells you immediately instead of retrying in circles.

settings.label: What Goals May Write
settings.desc: How much a goal can change directly — from read-only, to proposals, to its own isolated worktree, to a writing lease.

settings.label: Start Work Only When Ready
settings.desc: Work nodes start only once every required request is accepted — no half-started work. Atomic is the safe default.

settings.label: Receipt Log Handling
settings.desc: How raw logs inside goal receipts are stored: kept whole, with sensitive bits redacted, or capped in size. Receipts always keep summaries.

settings.label: Keep Evidence For (Days)
settings.desc: How long saved proof-of-work files stick around before cleanup. Leave empty to keep everything forever.

settings.label: Always Keep Last N Runs
settings.desc: Protects evidence from your most recent runs no matter how old it gets. Empty means no run-based limit.

settings.label: Prune Evidence During Cleanup
settings.desc: When you run 'Clean workspace now', also delete evidence past your retention rules. Off keeps cleanup conservative.

settings.label: Goal Evidence Detail
settings.desc: How much evidence goal mode saves as it works, from minimal notes to a full indefinite archive.

settings.label: Hide Sensitive Data In Evidence
settings.desc: Scrubs things like keys and personal data out of saved evidence and logs before they're stored.

settings.label: Back-Seat Driver Mode
settings.desc: Controls independent read-only run oversight. Off makes no advisory provider call, Auto evaluates only at governed risk or phase triggers, and On requests evaluation for every eligible run within quota.

settings.label: Use Git During Runs
settings.desc: Lets runs make branches, commits, and pull requests. Turn off to keep runs from touching version history at all.

settings.label: Main Branch Name
settings.desc: The branch all new work starts from and merges back into. Change only if your repo uses something other than main.

settings.label: Test Before Merging
settings.desc: Runs your project's tests before AI work is merged, and blocks the merge if they fail. Your best safety net against broken code.

settings.label: Open Pull Requests Automatically
settings.desc: Creates a GitHub pull request when a run finishes merging its branch, so finished work is ready for review without extra steps.

settings.label: When a Chat Is Deleted
settings.desc: What happens to a chat's private workspace when you delete the chat: ask you each time, keep it around, or remove it.

settings.label: Start Runs With a Clean Workspace
settings.desc: Removes stray untracked files before a run starts so leftovers from earlier attempts can't confuse the AI. Never touches app data.

settings.label: Clear Old Agent Output
settings.desc: Empties the agent-output folder before each run so results never mix with a previous run's files.

settings.label: Clean Workspace Now
settings.desc: One-click tidy-up that removes stray files right now, with a confirmation and an optional preview of what would be deleted.

settings.label: Workspace List Filter
settings.desc: Which workspaces show in the Source Control panel: everything, or only ones made by chats, the orchestrator, or you.

settings.label: Source Control Panel Sections
settings.desc: Which sections stay open in the Source Control panel. Purely a view preference — collapse what you never use.

settings.label: Pinned GitHub Workflows
settings.desc: GitHub Actions you pin to watch from inside the app, with branch and status badges. Pin the checks you care about most.

settings.label: Create a GitHub Repo for New Projects
settings.desc: When starting a brand-new project, also create its GitHub repository during setup so work can be pushed from day one.

settings.label: New Repo Details
settings.desc: Name, public/private visibility, description, .gitignore template, license, and starting branch for a repo created during setup.

settings.label: Upstream Repository
settings.desc: The original repo (URL or owner/repo) when you're building on or contributing back to someone else's project.

settings.label: Fork the Upstream Repo
settings.desc: Makes your own copy of the upstream repo automatically via GitHub so you can propose changes without write access.

settings.label: Fork URL or Path
settings.desc: Where your fork lives (clone URL or local path) once it exists. Filled in automatically when auto-fork is on.

settings.label: Contribution Branch Name
settings.desc: The branch your pull-request work goes on when contributing to another project, e.g. feature/add-x.

settings.label: How Finished Work Is Merged
settings.desc: Auto follows your project's convention; merge keeps history, squash makes one tidy commit, rebase replays commits. Merge is safest.

settings.label: When Commits Get Pushed
settings.desc: Manual means you push when ready; auto pushes after each successful merge; never keeps everything local until you say so.

settings.label: Allow Force Pushing
settings.desc: Force pushes can overwrite others' work. Never is safest; with-lease refuses if someone else pushed first; always is risky.

settings.label: Git Safety Level
settings.desc: One dial for how carefully the app handles branches and recovery. Strict double-checks everything; lenient asks less; custom uses your settings.

settings.label: Branch Naming Style
settings.desc: The workflow convention used when naming new branches — feature branches, hotfixes, releases, trunk-based, or your own scheme.

settings.label: Custom Branch Name Pattern
settings.desc: A template for generated branch names using {node} and {id} placeholders. Leave blank to use the naming style above.

settings.label: Workspace Folder Location
settings.desc: The folder on disk where private AI workspaces are created. Move it if your default drive is short on space.

settings.label: Private Workspace per Chat
settings.desc: Gives each new chat its own branch and workspace on the first message, so experiments never touch your main files until merged.

settings.label: Chat Workspaces Start From
settings.desc: The branch new chat workspaces are created from. Normally inherits your main branch — override for long-lived feature work.

settings.label: Manage This Chat's Workspace
settings.desc: Create, attach, merge, or open a pull request for the current chat's workspace, and see whether it's clean, dirty, or in conflict.

settings.label: File Browser Follows Active Chat
settings.desc: The file browser shows the files of whichever chat workspace you're in, so you always look at the version being edited.

settings.label: Test Command
settings.desc: The command run before merging. Auto-detect finds your project's test runner; set it yourself if detection picks wrong.

settings.label: Test Time Limit (Seconds)
settings.desc: How long pre-merge tests may run before being stopped (30–1800 s). Raise this if your test suite is genuinely slow.

settings.label: What Gets Tested Before Merge
settings.desc: Merged result tests your branch combined with the latest main — catches clashes early. Branch only is faster but can miss them.

settings.label: Too-Many-Workspaces Warning
settings.desc: Shows a gentle heads-up when this many workspaces pile up, since each one uses disk space. Set 0 to turn the warning off.

settings.label: Workspace Creation Time Limit (Seconds)
settings.desc: How long to wait for a new workspace before giving up (5–300 s). Raise it for very large repositories.

settings.label: Fix a Stuck Branch or Workspace
settings.desc: Guided recovery for tangled merges, orphaned workspaces, and other git trouble — undo safely instead of typing git commands.

settings.label: Auto-Refresh GitHub Checks
settings.desc: Keeps pinned workflow statuses current using event updates plus an occasional poll, so you don't have to hit refresh.

settings.label: Also Delete Ignored Files on Cleanup
settings.desc: Extends cleanup to gitignored files like caches and local configs. Off by default because those files can be hard to recreate.

settings.label: Delete Build Output After Runs
settings.desc: Removes known build folders (like target/) when a run ends to reclaim disk space, at the cost of slower rebuilds next time.

settings.label: Remove All Workspaces
settings.desc: Deletes every AI workspace in this project in one sweep. Use after big experiments; unmerged work in them is lost.

settings.label: Keep Run Evidence For (Days)
settings.desc: How many days of run logs and evidence to keep before old ones are deleted. Blank keeps everything forever.

settings.label: Or Keep Only the Last N Runs
settings.desc: Alternative to day-based cleanup: keep evidence for just the most recent runs. Blank keeps everything.

settings.label: Work as a Crew
settings.desc: Runs several AI models on your goal together instead of one. More perspectives and catches, but uses noticeably more credits.

settings.label: Crew Members
settings.desc: The ordered lineup of AI teammates, each with its own model and provider. First run confirms the model-to-provider pairing.

settings.label: Crews Running at Once
settings.desc: Requests a hard ceiling on crews running at once. The RuntimeResourceGovernor for the exact Host may reduce the admitted ceiling or queue or block work to protect that machine and its accounts.

settings.label: Agents per Crew
settings.desc: Requests a hard ceiling on active teammates in one crew. The RuntimeResourceGovernor for the exact Host may reduce the admitted ceiling or queue or block reviewer and worker spawns.

settings.label: Use Helper Agents
settings.desc: Lets the app bring in specialized helpers for each seam, package, lane, or node of a run. Turning off means one agent does everything.

settings.label: Run Helpers in Parallel
settings.desc: Lets helpers work side by side in separate workspaces instead of taking turns. Faster, but heavier on your machine and budget.

settings.label: Helpers Working at Once
settings.desc: Requests a hard ceiling on helper agents working simultaneously in one wave. The RuntimeResourceGovernor for the exact Host may reduce the admitted ceiling or queue or block helpers when capacity is constrained.

settings.label: Split Work Only When Big Enough
settings.desc: How complex a job must be before it's split among helpers. Higher means fewer helpers and lower cost on small jobs.

settings.label: Max Reading per Helper (Tokens)
settings.desc: Caps how much material each helper is handed, keeping costs predictable and forcing focused assignments.

settings.label: If a Helper Fails
settings.desc: Whether failed helpers get another try. Bounded retries gives a couple of attempts; backoff waits longer between tries.

settings.label: Always Use Helpers
settings.desc: Forces helper agents on every run instead of letting the app decide when they're worth it. Usually best left off.

settings.label: One Writer at a Time
settings.desc: Only one agent may change files at any moment, preventing two helpers from overwriting each other's edits.

settings.label: Extra Helper Write Protection
settings.desc: Optionally restrict helpers further: only the lead writes, helpers propose patches, or each helper gets its own isolated workspace.

settings.label: Pick Helpers per Step Type
settings.desc: Choose exactly which helpers run at each step type (seam, package, lane, iteration). Empty lists let the app choose automatically.

settings.label: Always Include These Helpers
settings.desc: Helpers that join every run no matter what. This list wins even over the excluded list below.

settings.label: Never Use These Helpers
settings.desc: Helpers excluded from automatic selection — useful when one keeps getting picked but never helps your project.

settings.label: Simultaneous Requests per AI Provider
settings.desc: Requests a hard ceiling on parallel calls to one provider. The RuntimeResourceGovernor for the exact Host may reduce the admitted ceiling or queue or block calls for current host capacity and provider limits; a run may request a lower override.

settings.label: Total Agents Active at Once
settings.desc: Requests a hard ceiling on all active agents across crews and helpers. The RuntimeResourceGovernor for the exact Host may reduce the admitted ceiling or queue or block work as the final protection for that machine.

settings.label: How Deep Helpers Can Delegate
settings.desc: How many levels of helpers-hiring-helpers are allowed before the run is stopped. Prevents runaway chains of agents.

settings.label: Total Agents per Run
settings.desc: A run is stopped once it has created this many agents in total — the emergency brake against runaway spawning costs.

settings.label: Helpers Hiring Their Own Helpers
settings.desc: How many further levels a helper may delegate. 0 means helpers must do their own work — the safest and cheapest choice.

settings.label: View Agent Permissions Snapshot
settings.desc: Shows the frozen rulebook each agent gets before its first call: autonomy, what it may write, model policy, tool limits, budgets.

settings.label: View Helper Work Contract
settings.desc: Shows the contract a helper works under — its parent goal, allowed step, read/write mode, and how results are returned.

settings.label: Keep Helper Memory Separate
settings.desc: Each helper keeps its own context and cache, and its errors surface as clean failures instead of corrupting the main run.

settings.label: Track Imported Agents' Origins
settings.desc: Records where outside agents came from, what they were allowed to do, and their transcripts — an audit trail for borrowed help.

settings.label: Image Generation Service
settings.desc: Which service creates images for chat, artifacts, and web content. Options that your plan or route can't use are shown greyed out with a reason.

settings.label: Model Per Media Task
settings.desc: Pick a specific model for each kind of media job (images vs diagrams vs video) instead of using the service's default.

settings.label: Media Model Nicknames
settings.desc: Shorthand names that map to full model IDs (e.g. 'nano banana' → gemini-2.5-flash-image). Changes lookups only, not what a model can do.

settings.label: Accept Media Input
settings.desc: Let the app take in images, screenshots, and other media you attach. Turn off to keep runs text-only.

settings.label: Allow Media Output
settings.desc: Let runs hand back images, audio, and other files — not just text. Turn off if you only ever want written results.

settings.label: Allow Voice Input
settings.desc: Speak instead of type: your voice becomes a draft message you can review before sending.

settings.label: Understand Images & Screenshots
settings.desc: Lets the app 'see' images and screenshots you share, even when the working model can't, by routing them through a vision helper.

settings.label: Where Screenshots Come From
settings.desc: Where the app looks first when you say 'look at my screenshot': your clipboard, recent OS captures, or asking you to pick.

settings.label: Image Lookup Order
settings.desc: When several images could match your request, this order decides which wins: attachments, artifacts, project files, clipboard, or screenshots.

settings.label: Backup Model for Images
settings.desc: Which model steps in when your usual vision model is down or unavailable. 'Auto' picks the best available one for you.

settings.label: If Screenshot Blurring Fails
settings.desc: Sensitive info in screenshots is blurred before models see it. If blurring fails, either block the image (safer) or let you override.

settings.label: Keep Generated Files For
settings.desc: How long generated media and other outputs are kept before cleanup. Note: some provider download links expire after 24 hours regardless.

settings.label: Where Outputs Are Saved
settings.desc: The folder inside your project where generated media and files land. Change it if you want outputs somewhere easier to find.

settings.label: Media Generation
settings.desc: The master switch for creating images, video, speech, and music. When off, the app may suggest media but never actually generates it.

settings.label: What Can Be Generated
settings.desc: Choose which media kinds are allowed: images, screenshots, diagrams, recordings, video. Anything off reports 'disabled by admin' to tools.

settings.label: Video Generation
settings.desc: Allow creating short video clips. Not every backend supports this — unsupported ones will refuse with a clear error.

settings.label: Speech Generation
settings.desc: Allow turning text into spoken audio. May be locked off by a workspace admin on some plans.

settings.label: Music Generation
settings.desc: Allow creating songs, instrumentals, and beats. Off by default since most projects never need it.

settings.label: Image Shape
settings.desc: Default shape for generated images: square, widescreen, or tall. You can still override it per request; MiniMax also takes exact pixel sizes.

settings.label: Image Size
settings.desc: How big generated images are. Bigger looks sharper but costs more and takes longer.

settings.label: Image Quality
settings.desc: Trade speed for polish: draft is fast and cheap, high takes longer and costs more.

settings.label: Images Per Request
settings.desc: How many variations to generate each time (1–8). More options to pick from, but each one costs credits.

settings.label: Video Length (Seconds)
settings.desc: Default length of generated clips (0.5–60s). Longer videos take much longer and cost more.

settings.label: Video Resolution
settings.desc: Sharpness of generated video. This wins over any pixel-size hint when both are given.

settings.label: Speech Voice
settings.desc: Which voice reads generated speech aloud. Pick one that suits your project's tone.

settings.label: Image File Format
settings.desc: File type for saved images. PNG is lossless; JPG and WebP are smaller files.

settings.label: How Images Are Delivered
settings.desc: Get images back as a link or as embedded data. Heads-up: MiniMax links expire after 24 hours, so download what you want to keep.

settings.label: Repeatable Results (Seed)
settings.desc: Set a number to get the same image from the same prompt every time. Leave blank for a fresh random result each run.

settings.label: Auto-Improve Image Prompts
settings.desc: Lets MiniMax rewrite your prompt for better images. Off keeps your exact wording, which is more predictable.

settings.label: Music Tempo (BPM)
settings.desc: Default beats-per-minute for generated music (60–200). 120 is a comfortable middle for most styles.

settings.label: Service-Specific Options
settings.desc: Raw extra options passed to your media service, for anything not covered by the controls above. Leave empty unless a guide tells you.

settings.label: Let the AI Search the Web
settings.desc: Allows web searches in chat (and the /web command). Turn off if you never want the AI reaching the internet during a run.

settings.label: Web Provider Order
settings.desc: Who answers web requests first, and who covers when they fail. Reorder if a provider is slow or you prefer another service.

settings.label: Provider Connection Status
settings.desc: Shows whether each web service is connected, needs a key, or recently failed - so you know why a search fell back or stopped. Keys live in your system keychain and are never shown here.

settings.label: Show Provider Health Details
settings.desc: Adds last-failure messages and error detail to each provider row. Turn off for a quieter settings page.

settings.label: DuckDuckGo Fallback
settings.desc: Keyless backup search used when paid providers are unavailable. Results are basic (plain page scraping) but always free.

settings.label: Firecrawl Provider
settings.desc: A heavier crawler for tough or JavaScript-heavy sites. Stays off until you add an API key or a self-hosted address below.

settings.label: Firecrawl API Key
settings.desc: Paste your key from firecrawl.dev to turn Firecrawl on. Stored in your computer's secure credential store, never in plain files.

settings.label: Firecrawl Server Address
settings.desc: Point at your own Firecrawl server instead of the cloud (no credit billing). The app never switches between them silently.

settings.label: Exa Provider
settings.desc: A search-first service that shines at web search and deep research runs. Covers: search, research, and page extraction. Support level: partner adapter.

settings.label: Tavily Provider
settings.desc: A balanced service covering search, page reading, and extraction. Tune how deeply it reads with the setting below. Support level: partner adapter.

settings.label: Tavily Reading Depth
settings.desc: How hard Tavily works when reading a page. Light modes are fast and cheap; advanced digs deeper but costs more per page.

settings.label: Brave Search Provider
settings.desc: An independent search index used for web search only. Stays off until you add an API key. Support level: community adapter.

settings.label: Jina Reader Provider
settings.desc: A page-reading service used for fetching and extracting stubborn pages. Stays off until you add an API key. Support level: community adapter.

settings.label: Model-Native Web Tools
settings.desc: Lets models that ship their own web search answer directly through your existing model account - no extra key needed. Sits last in the fallback chain.

settings.label: Operation Coverage & Fallback
settings.desc: Which service answers each web operation first, and the fallback path behind it. Every operation card shows what actually ran (requested vs effective) plus cache state and credit warnings.

settings.label: Manage Web Access Keys
settings.desc: Create, list, or revoke the keys used for web operations. Revoke immediately if a key may have leaked.

settings.label: PDF Reading Mode
settings.desc: How web PDFs are read. Auto picks the best method; OCR handles scanned documents but is slower. Can be overridden per request.

settings.label: Search Results per Query
settings.desc: How many results a web search returns. More results give broader answers but cost more time and provider credits.

settings.label: Research: Max Sources
settings.desc: Caps how many different sites a research task pulls from, keeping deep-dives fast and affordable.

settings.label: Research: Pages Read Automatically
settings.desc: How many pages research may open without asking you. Above this cap, the AI checks in before reading more.

settings.label: Crawl: Max Pages
settings.desc: Caps pages fetched when crawling a whole site. The app's cap (25) deliberately overrides Firecrawl's huge 10,000-page default.

settings.label: Crawl: Max Link Depth
settings.desc: How many clicks away from the starting page a crawl may wander. Deeper crawls find more but take much longer.

settings.label: Site Map: Max Pages
settings.desc: Caps pages listed when mapping a site's structure (listing URLs without reading them).

settings.label: Site Map: Max Depth
settings.desc: How deep site mapping follows links when listing a site's pages.

settings.label: Page Fetch Timeout
settings.desc: How long to wait for one page (in ms). Batch fetches wait timeout × min(count, 5), capped at 600s, so big jobs can't hang forever.

settings.label: Ask Before Spending Credits
settings.desc: Web jobs estimated above this many provider credits pause and ask you first. Lower it if bills surprise you.

settings.label: Credit Hard Cap
settings.desc: Web jobs above this credit estimate are blocked outright; you must approve that specific operation to proceed.

settings.label: Provider-Side Caching
settings.desc: Lets Firecrawl reuse its own cached copies of pages. Off keeps results freshest; the app's own cache always takes precedence.

settings.label: Web Cache Size (MB)
settings.desc: Disk space for saved web pages per project, so repeat reads are instant and free. Oldest entries are dropped when full.

settings.label: Cache Lifetime: Searches (s)
settings.desc: How long saved search results stay fresh before being fetched again. Searches go stale fastest, so this is the shortest.

settings.label: Cache Lifetime: Pages (s)
settings.desc: How long saved page content stays fresh before being re-fetched.

settings.label: Cache Lifetime: Crawls (s)
settings.desc: How long saved crawl and site-map results stay fresh. Longest lifetime, since site structure rarely changes.

settings.label: Firecrawl Anti-Block Mode
settings.desc: How aggressively Firecrawl dodges site blocking. Basic is cheapest; enhanced costs +4 credits per page. Cloud only.

settings.label: Browser Session Type
settings.desc: Ordinary Browser Program sessions may use a persistent project profile or an isolated clean profile. Protected AuthBrowserSession is always ephemeral and is not affected by this setting.

settings.label: Remember Website Logins
settings.desc: For ordinary Browser Program sessions only, saves policy-approved cookies and site data for later ordinary runs. Protected AuthBrowserSession never saves or restores state regardless of this value.

settings.label: Follow Redirects From Custom Servers
settings.desc: Whether custom provider servers may redirect requests elsewhere. Deny is safest — it blocks traffic to hosts you never approved.

settings.label: Custom Server Timeout (s)
settings.desc: Cuts off slow custom provider servers after this many seconds; each cutoff is recorded in the run's transport receipt.

settings.label: Network Proxy
settings.desc: How the app reaches the internet: your computer's proxy settings, a custom proxy you enter below, or no proxy at all.

settings.label: HTTP Proxy Address
settings.desc: Proxy for plain web traffic. Only used when Network Proxy is set to manual.

settings.label: HTTPS Proxy Address
settings.desc: Proxy for secure web traffic. Only used when Network Proxy is set to manual.

settings.label: Skip Proxy for These Sites
settings.desc: Domains that connect directly, bypassing the proxy — usually internal company addresses. One per line or comma-separated.

settings.label: Proxy Sign-In Details
settings.desc: Username and password for proxies that require them. Kept only in your computer's secure credential store, never plain text.

settings.label: Custom Certificate File
settings.desc: A company-issued certificate bundle for networks that inspect traffic. The app checks it and warns before certificates expire.

settings.label: Per-Site Certificate Overrides
settings.desc: Use a specific certificate only for particular hosts, leaving all other traffic on normal trust rules.

settings.label: Offline (Air-Gap) Mode
settings.desc: Blocks all network use by policy. Errors then clearly say whether something was cached, blocked, unreachable, or untrusted.

settings.label: Project Search Index
settings.desc: Keeps a fast index of your project so search and autocomplete are instant. Turning it off cancels any build and clears partial data.

settings.label: Rebuild Search Index
settings.desc: Throws away the index and builds it fresh, with progress shown. Use when search results look stale or wrong.

settings.label: View Index Disk Usage
settings.desc: Shows how much space the index uses locally and (for remote projects) on the remote side, before you decide to clear it.

settings.label: Skip Files Larger Than (MB)
settings.desc: Big files are left out of the index to keep it fast. Raise this only if you genuinely need to search huge files.

settings.label: Files to Leave Out of Search
settings.desc: Patterns for generated or junk files the index should skip, added on top of built-in defaults. Fewer junk hits, faster search.

settings.label: Follow Shortcut Links When Indexing
settings.desc: Lets indexing follow symlinked folders. Off by default for safety — linked paths must still stay inside your project.

settings.label: Remote Project Cache
settings.desc: For remote projects only: index a lighter slice locally to speed up first indexing of big projects. Hidden for local projects.

settings.label: Clear Index Cache
settings.desc: Frees the disk space the index uses, after showing usage and asking you to confirm. Search rebuilds it next time it's needed.

settings.label: Default Persona
settings.desc: The character that answers when you have not picked one. It sets the style, model, and habits of everyday replies.

settings.label: Manage Personas
settings.desc: Create, edit, disable, restore, or reorder your cast. Core personas stay read-only; your own are fully editable.

settings.label: Persona for This Chat
settings.desc: Which character is speaking right now, and why it was chosen. Change it here or just ask for someone else in plain words.

settings.label: Who Picks the Persona
settings.desc: Let the app choose the best character for each request, pick one yourself, or mix: auto-pick unless you override.

settings.label: Ask for a Persona in Plain Words
settings.desc: Type things like "let the researcher handle this" to switch characters mid-run. It never changes accounts or sign-ins.

settings.label: Built-In Core Personas
settings.desc: The nine protected characters that ship with the app. They cannot be edited or removed, so things always work.

settings.label: Keep This Persona
settings.desc: Stops the app from switching characters between turns. Turn off to let auto-selection take over again.

settings.label: Hidden Specialty Personas
settings.desc: Tuck away bundled specialists you never use so pickers stay short. Restore them any time with one click.

settings.label: Where New Personas Live
settings.desc: Save new characters just for this project or for every project. Project-local personas override global ones with the same job.

settings.label: Persona Name
settings.desc: The friendly display name shown in pickers and chat, up to 100 characters.

settings.label: Persona Description
settings.desc: A short blurb (up to 500 characters) explaining what this character is good at, shown when browsing the library.

settings.label: Persona ID
settings.desc: The unique lowercase-with-dashes name used in files and automation. It must match its folder and cannot copy a core persona.

settings.label: Persona Tags
settings.desc: Labels like seam, package, lane, node, language, or domain that help search and auto-selection find the right character.

settings.label: Persona Nicknames
settings.desc: Other names this character answers to, so "ask the prof" can reach your teacher persona.

settings.label: Persona's Preferred Model
settings.desc: The AI model this character uses when active. Leave empty to inherit whatever the project or app already picked.

settings.label: Response Style
settings.desc: The overall voice of this character: short and to the point, thorough, or somewhere in between.

settings.label: Talkativeness
settings.desc: Nudges how chatty this character is, without changing the model itself. Plan mode leans chattier, agent mode quieter.

settings.label: Answer Length
settings.desc: How long answers run: terse bullet points, normal, or verbose with full explanations. Docs disagreed on wording; terse|normal|verbose wins.

settings.label: Answer Format
settings.desc: The shape of replies: formatted text, raw data, or plain unstyled text. Docs disagreed on choices; markdown is the safe default.

settings.label: Persona's Starting Mode
settings.desc: How this character begins working: ask before acting, plan first, work normally, or run without pauses. Runs can still override it.

settings.label: Persona's Preferred Provider
settings.desc: Which AI service this character prefers, like Claude, Gemini Direct, or Antigravity CLI. Leave empty to inherit.

settings.label: Persona's Speed vs Power
settings.desc: Prefer the fast or the powerful edition of the chosen model family. Leave empty to inherit.

settings.label: Creativity
settings.desc: Higher values make this character more inventive but less predictable. Leave at the model's default unless replies feel too stiff or too random.

settings.label: Word Choice Range
settings.desc: Limits how far the model wanders when picking words. Most people never need to change this; it stacks with Creativity.

settings.label: Thinking Effort
settings.desc: How hard this character thinks before answering. More effort means smarter answers but slower and pricier runs.

settings.label: Spending Cap per Persona
settings.desc: A cost ceiling for this character. Models over budget are skipped with a note and a cheaper suggestion, never silently.

settings.label: How Eagerly Tools Are Used
settings.desc: Whether this character reaches for tools: never, only when clearly needed, or at every chance. Docs disagreed; auto is the safe pick.

settings.label: Favorite Tools
settings.desc: Tools this character reaches for first, like Site Reader for the web. Guidance only; permissions still apply.

settings.label: Tools to Avoid
settings.desc: Tools this character skips unless nothing else works. It is a nudge, not a ban; use permissions to truly block a tool.

settings.label: Tool-Use Notes
settings.desc: Freeform advice on when and how this character should pick tools, written in plain English.

settings.label: Custom Instructions
settings.desc: The written personality and rules injected whenever this character runs. A compiled preview shows exactly what the AI will see.

settings.label: Skills This Persona Carries
settings.desc: Skill packs loaded automatically whenever this character is active, so it always knows its specialty tricks.

settings.label: Permission Profile
settings.desc: The named rule set deciding what this character may do without asking you first. Leave empty to inherit the project's rules.

settings.label: Plugins Turned Off for This Persona
settings.desc: Plugins this character ignores while working. They stay installed and keep running for everyone else.

settings.label: Show What the Model Supports
settings.desc: Marks each tuning control as fully, partly, or not supported by the current model, so you know which knobs actually work.

settings.label: See Which Settings Were Skipped
settings.desc: Opens a log of persona settings the model could not honor on recent runs, so surprises are never silent.

settings.label: Your Skills
settings.desc: Add, import, edit, or remove the add-on abilities agents can use. Removing asks for confirmation so nothing disappears by accident.

settings.label: Turn Skills On or Off
settings.desc: Switch any single skill on or off without deleting it. Off skills stay installed but agents can't use them.

settings.label: Skills Panel in Chat
settings.desc: Lets you type /skill in chat to browse and run skills without opening Settings. Skills can also be called by name in plain English.

settings.label: Find Skills Automatically
settings.desc: Scans your project and computer for skill folders on startup. When two skills share a name, the project copy wins.

settings.label: Rescan for Skills
settings.desc: Looks again in all skill folders right now — use after adding files by hand or pulling new project changes.

settings.label: Skill Info Badges
settings.desc: Shows whether each skill is ready to use, where it came from, and which personas rely on it — so surprises are visible up front.

settings.label: Which Skills to Show
settings.desc: Controls the skill list filter. 'Active only' keeps the list tidy; an alternate draft proposed Basic/Advanced/All grouping instead.

settings.label: Sort Skill List
settings.desc: Orders the skill list by name, where it came from, or its permission — remembered for the rest of this session.

settings.label: Search Skills
settings.desc: Type to narrow the skill list by name, description, source, readiness, or permission — handy once you have many installed.

settings.label: Preview a Skill
settings.desc: Opens a read-only view of a skill's instructions so you can see exactly what it will do before letting it run.

settings.label: Skill Permissions
settings.desc: Decide per skill (or name pattern like doc-*) whether it runs freely, is blocked, or asks you first. Exact names beat patterns.

settings.label: Set Permissions by Pattern
settings.desc: Applies one permission to every skill matching a pattern (like doc-*) at once; shows how many will change before you confirm.

settings.label: Let Skills Run Automatically
settings.desc: Ready skills may start on their own when relevant. Skills with warnings always wait for you to pick them yourself.

settings.label: Auto-Enable New Skills
settings.desc: Turns freshly installed skills on immediately. Kept off so nothing new runs until you've had a look at it.

settings.label: Check All Skills for Problems
settings.desc: Scans every skill for broken headers, name mismatches, or overlong descriptions and lists anything that needs fixing.

settings.label: Share Skills with Other Agent Tools
settings.desc: Copies your skills into folders other AI tools read (.claude/skills, .agents/skills) so the same abilities work everywhere.

settings.label: Skill Sharing Method
settings.desc: Copy makes an independent duplicate; symlink keeps one shared original but only works on file systems that support links.

settings.label: Skill Catalog Size Limit (%)
settings.desc: Caps how much of the model's working memory the skill list may fill. Skills left out are shown in the prompt inspector.

settings.label: Skill Catalog Size Limit (Characters)
settings.desc: Hard character cap for the skill and tool listing sent to the model — the tighter of this and the % limit applies.

settings.label: Plugins On or Off
settings.desc: Switch each plugin on or off — per persona too, so one helper can use a plugin others don't. Off plugins never load.

settings.label: Install Plugin from Catalog
settings.desc: Downloads a plugin by name and version from the catalog and reloads the app's plugin list when it finishes.

settings.label: Add Plugin from Your Computer
settings.desc: Points the app at a plugin folder on disk — useful for trying a plugin someone shared before it's published anywhere.

settings.label: Remove Plugin
settings.desc: Uninstalls a plugin. Ones you added from disk offer 'Delete from disk' with a confirmation so files aren't lost silently.

settings.label: Which Plugins to Show
settings.desc: Controls the plugin list filter, plus readiness and capability notes. An alternate draft proposed Basic/Advanced/All grouping.

settings.label: Auto-Enable New Plugins
settings.desc: Turns freshly installed plugins on immediately. Kept off so new code never hooks into the app without your say-so.

settings.label: Plugin Package List
settings.desc: The full list of plugin packages to load — catalog names like name@1.0 or folders on disk. No passwords are ever stored here.

settings.label: Plugin Time Limit (ms)
settings.desc: How long a plugin may run at each hook point before it's cut off (100–30000 ms). Raise only if a trusted plugin needs more time.

settings.label: Let Plugins Replace Built-In Tools
settings.desc: Allows plugins to change how the app's own tools behave. Off by default for stability — a warning shows whenever it's on.

settings.label: Keyboard Shortcuts
settings.desc: See every action's key combo and change any of them. Only your changes are saved; clashes are flagged before they cause trouble.

settings.label: Shortcut Hints & Cheat Sheet
settings.desc: Shows key combos next to buttons and offers an in-app cheat sheet — the easiest way to pick up shortcuts as you go.

settings.label: Search Shortcuts
settings.desc: Find any shortcut by typing the action's name or the key combo itself — faster than scrolling the full list.

settings.label: Custom Slash Commands
settings.desc: Create your own /commands for things you type often — saved app-wide or just for this project. Built-ins can't be replaced here.

settings.label: When Shortcuts Clash
settings.desc: What happens if two actions share a key combo: warn you (safest), hide the newer one, or let the newer one take over.

settings.label: Text Editing Keys
settings.desc: The key combos for moving and deleting inside the chat box — jump to line start/end, delete words, and more. Each is remappable.

settings.label: Reset Shortcuts to Defaults
settings.desc: Puts one shortcut — or all of them — back to the factory setup. Resetting everything asks for confirmation first.

settings.label: Export or Import Shortcuts
settings.desc: Saves your shortcut setup to a file, or loads one — choosing to replace everything or merge with what you have.

settings.label: Model Variant Cycling Key
settings.desc: Optional key combo to flip between model variants without opening the picker; also available from the command palette.

settings.label: Where a Command Lives
settings.desc: Choose whether a new command is available everywhere or only inside this project's own commands folder.

settings.label: Command Freedom Level
settings.desc: How much a command's run may do on its own: ask first, plan only, run normally, or skip all confirmations ('yolo').

settings.label: Command Model Override
settings.desc: Make a specific command always use a particular AI model instead of whatever the current chat is using.

settings.label: Command Persona Override
settings.desc: Make a specific command always run as a particular persona, regardless of who is active in the chat.

settings.label: Command Permissions Override
settings.desc: Give a specific command its own safety profile — for example, a stricter one for anything that touches your files.

settings.label: Replace a Built-In Command
settings.desc: Expert-only: lets a custom command take over a built-in name. Core commands like /web, /skill, and /stop can never be replaced.

settings.label: Git Command Routing
settings.desc: Keeps /git and /github pointed at the built-in version-control helpers. These names are reserved and can't be taken over.

settings.label: Check My Setup
settings.desc: Runs a full checkup of connections, storage, sign-ins, and tools, then shows fixes for anything that is not ready.

settings.label: Capability Provisioning
settings.desc: Controls setup of non-provider capabilities for the exact Host and Environment. Off forbids provisioning, Auto provisions only after policy checks pass, and On requires availability without waiving those checks; provider CLI first acquisition is excluded and always requires explicit official-source setup.

settings.label: Setup Health Summary
settings.desc: A read-only snapshot of your last checkup: Ready, Ready with Warnings, or Blocked. Open it to see exactly what to fix.

settings.label: Check Automatically
settings.desc: Lets the app quietly re-run its checkup on a schedule so problems are caught before they interrupt your work.

settings.label: How Often to Check
settings.desc: How often the automatic checkup runs. Daily is a good balance; pick Never if you prefer to run checks yourself.

settings.label: What the Checkup Covers
settings.desc: Choose which areas get checked. Turning areas off makes checks faster but can hide real problems.

settings.label: Show Ready/Not-Ready Badges
settings.desc: Shows small status labels (Ready, Needs setup, Needs attention) around the app so you can spot problems at a glance.

settings.label: Warn About Failing Connections
settings.desc: Surfaces stale or partly broken pieces (like a flaky tool server or locked file safety) instead of hiding them until they fail.

settings.label: Show Fix-It Links
settings.desc: Adds a direct "fix this" link next to each failed check so you can jump straight to the setting that solves it.

settings.label: Share Usage Data
settings.desc: Sends anonymous usage and crash reports to help improve the app. Off by default — nothing leaves your computer unless you opt in.

settings.label: Run Deep Diagnostics
settings.desc: Collects detailed info about your computer and app install. Useful when support asks for it; you rarely need it otherwise.

settings.label: Connected Tool Servers
settings.desc: Every outside tool server in one list, with a plain status per row: Working, Not Configured, Needs Auth, Untrusted Folder, Unhealthy, Install Failed, Unsupported, or External.…

settings.label: Turn a Server On or Off
settings.desc: Switches one server on or off without deleting it. Off means the app never loads it, even if it is fully set up.

settings.label: Turn Single Tools On or Off
settings.desc: Pick which individual tools from a server your helpers may use. Separate from permissions — off means invisible, not just blocked.

settings.label: Importing Servers From Other Apps
settings.desc: When servers are found in other apps' configs (Claude, Codex, Warp), ask before importing and review them first. Sources and secrets are tracked and redacted.

settings.label: Server Health & Logs
settings.desc: See when each server was last checked and its last error. Read-only — a quick way to tell why a tool stopped responding.

settings.label: Sign Out of a Server
settings.desc: Revokes a server's saved sign-in without deleting the server. Use this if credentials expire or you suspect a leak.

settings.label: How a Server Connects
settings.desc: The connection style for each server: a local program (stdio) or a web address (sse or http). Each server uses exactly one.

settings.label: Server Launch Details
settings.desc: The command, arguments, folder, and environment used to start a local server. Wrong values here are the top cause of Install Failed.

settings.label: Remote Server Address
settings.desc: The web address for a remote server. Changing it wipes saved sign-ins for that server, so you will need to sign in again.

settings.label: Remote Server Headers
settings.desc: Extra key-value headers sent to a remote server, usually an API key. Used by servers that skip the normal sign-in flow.

settings.label: Detect Sign-In Automatically
settings.desc: Lets the app figure out a server's sign-in flow for you. Turn off only for servers that use a plain API key instead.

settings.label: Refresh a Server Sign-In
settings.desc: Forces a fresh sign-in token for a server right now. Handy when a server says Needs Auth but you already signed in.

settings.label: Where a Server Is Available
settings.desc: Whether a server is available everywhere, in one project, for one profile, or managed by another app (External). Each server has exactly one.

settings.label: Server Response Time Limit
settings.desc: How long (in milliseconds) to wait for a server to start or answer before giving up and recording the failure. Lower is snappier but flakier.

settings.label: Load Tool Details Only When Needed
settings.desc: Shares each tool's full details with the AI only when it is about to be used. Keeps prompts small and responses faster and cheaper.

settings.label: Tool List Refresh Interval
settings.desc: How long the app remembers a server's tool list before asking again. It also refreshes when you change settings or ask manually.

settings.label: Runtime Secret Injection
settings.desc: Lets approved secrets be added to server requests at run time only. They are hidden in logs, receipted, and can never grant extra access.

settings.label: Show Server Status in the App
settings.desc: Displays a live connected/disconnected indicator for tool servers around the app, not just on this page.

settings.label: Inspect Effective Server Config
settings.desc: A read-only view of exactly what settings each server ended up with, where each value came from, and its sign-in state.

settings.label: Check for App Updates
settings.desc: Looks for new versions of Puppet Master automatically. You are always asked before anything installs.

settings.label: Check for Content Updates
settings.desc: Keeps community add-ons (templates, personas, presets) up to date by checking the catalog for new versions.

settings.label: Update Check Frequency
settings.desc: How often the app looks for updates. You can always check manually regardless of this setting.

settings.label: Update Channel
settings.desc: Stable gets well-tested releases; Canary and Nightly get new features sooner but break more often. Affects update signing checks too.

settings.label: Reset Settings to Defaults
settings.desc: Puts one setting, a whole section, or everything back to factory values. Always asks first, and highlights what changed.

settings.label: Export or Back Up Settings
settings.desc: Saves your settings as a bundle file you can keep as a backup or move to another computer.

settings.label: Import Settings
settings.desc: Loads a settings bundle from a file. It is checked first, then you choose Replace or Merge — nothing is applied silently.

settings.label: Debug Mode
settings.desc: Records extra technical detail about what the app is doing. Slows things slightly; turn on only when chasing a problem.

settings.label: Log Detail Level
settings.desc: How chatty the app's logs are, from Silent to Trace. More detail helps support but fills disk faster.

settings.label: Activity Receipt Detail
settings.desc: How much detail the app keeps in its record of every action. Verbose gives a richer history but is noisier to read.

settings.label: Inspect Working Files
settings.desc: Shows the temporary files and internal artifacts the app creates while running. For debugging odd behavior only.

settings.label: Cursor App Location
settings.desc: Normally found automatically. Set a manual path only if the app cannot find your Cursor install; bad paths fail immediately.

settings.label: Claude Code App Location
settings.desc: Normally found automatically. Set a manual path only if the app cannot find your Claude Code install; bad paths fail immediately.

settings.label: Find Installed Apps Again
settings.desc: Re-searches your computer for coding apps from scratch, ignoring remembered locations. Use after installing or moving an app.

settings.label: Check Versions Match at Startup
settings.desc: Confirms the app's parts (desktop, background service, CLIs) are compatible before starting. Blocks with a clear message if not.

settings.label: Graphics Engine
settings.desc: How the app draws its windows. Auto picks the best for your computer; change only if you see visual glitches. Some plans listed this under Terminal instead.

settings.label: Read-Only Mode
settings.desc: Opens the app in look-but-don't-touch mode when its data store is locked by another copy. Prevents two copies from clobbering each other.

settings.label: Settings File Format
settings.desc: The file format used when settings are written to disk (yaml, json, or jsonc). Files are validated on load either way.

settings.label: Accept Old Config File Names
settings.desc: Lets projects made with older versions still load by recognizing retired config file names, with help text explaining the migration.

settings.label: Prompt Cache Checker
settings.desc: Watches for changes that would quietly break AI prompt caching (and raise your costs), and flags them before they ship.

settings.label: Chat History Retention
settings.desc: Read-only effective policy: canonical chat content and edit history are kept indefinitely while the thread exists. At 250,000 events, history rolls into a linked successor instead of silently evicting content; thread deletion follows the storage-owned purge and legal-hold rules.

settings.label: Runtime History Retention (Days)
settings.desc: Keeps run, node, attempt, remediation, worktree, lane, and runtime lifecycle history for at least 365 days after run completion. The default and owner minimum are 365; larger values are allowed, while a lower value is rejected with the storage-owner reason rather than silently raised.

settings.label: Ordinary Diagnostic History (Days)
settings.desc: Keeps ordinary and debug diagnostic history for at least 30 days. The default and owner minimum are 30; larger values are allowed, while a lower value is rejected with the storage-owner reason. This setting cannot shorten fixed security, approval, audit, migration, recovery, receipt, deletion, or other authority retention.

settings.label: Released Safe-Point Retention (Days)
settings.desc: Keeps an ordinary safe point for at least 90 days after its last hold or reference is released. The default and owner minimum are 90; larger values are allowed, while a lower value is rejected with the storage-owner reason. Anchored, referenced, preserved-run, and legally held safe points remain protected regardless of age.

settings.label: Automatically Preserved Terminal Runs
settings.desc: Read-only effective policy: each project automatically preserves its latest 25 terminal runs. When a run becomes the 26th-oldest, only its automatic recent-run anchor clears; manual keep, unresolved recovery, legal hold, audit, promotion, evidence, and other anchors remain independent.

settings.label: Request Storage Compaction
settings.desc: When available, routes an owner-admitted maintenance request through cmd.storage.compaction.request. The storage owner still evaluates eligibility, holds, anchors, references, gates, and the maintenance lease; this request cannot force compaction or bypass any of them.

settings.label: Inspect Legal Holds & Quarantine
settings.desc: Opens the read-only legal-hold and invalid-value quarantine view with effective scope, reasons, custody state, and recovery status. It never sets or clears a hold and never exports, purges, or resets quarantined bytes; hold mutation remains the protected cmd.storage.legal_hold.manage action authorized by storage.legal_hold.manage.

settings.label: Working Animation
settings.desc: Which animation the assistant shows while it is working: Orbit is the default richer view, Step Rail is the simplified list. Applies instantly and changes nothing about the work itself.

settings.label: Chat Title Model
settings.desc: Which model names your chats. Default lets the resolver pick a cheap fast one, None leaves every chat called New chat, or pick a specific available model. Renaming a chat yourself locks the name until you ask for a new one.

settings.label: Explain Terms Everywhere
settings.desc: Turns term explanations on for every new chat. The per-chat toggle still wins for a chat you have changed. Never changes generated documents.

settings.label: Plan Depth
settings.desc: How much work a Plan does before writing the document: Quick for a fast sketch, Standard for the usual balance, Thorough for careful analysis. All three produce the same read-only Plan document plus To-Dos.

settings.label: Deep Plan Depth
settings.desc: How much work a Deep Plan does: Thorough, Exhaustive, or BrainStorm. BrainStorm is a superset of Exhaustive that adds independent proposals, debate, and voting.

settings.label: Grill Me By Default
settings.desc: Starts every Deep Plan with Grill Me checked, which lets the workflow ask you more questions before planning. You can still toggle it per Plan.

settings.label: Plan Export Format
settings.desc: Which format the Plan export button produces first. Both PDF and Markdown stay available on every Plan.

settings.label: Keep Unsent Messages
settings.desc: Keeps whatever you typed and attached in each chat when you switch away, close, or crash. There is no draft banner and nothing to restore by hand -- the text is simply there when you come back.

settings.label: Crew Size
settings.desc: How many teammates a new Crew starts with. You can add or remove members in the Crew setup before it runs.

settings.label: Crew Coordinator
settings.desc: Who directs the Crew: the assistant you are already talking to, a dedicated coordinator teammate, or nobody (each member works its own assignment).

settings.label: Crew Assignment
settings.desc: How work is handed out: the manager directs it, members claim it, or everyone gets the same task for comparison.

settings.label: Crew Parallelism
settings.desc: How many Crew members may work at the same time. The host may still admit fewer.

settings.label: Crew Auto
settings.desc: Lets the assistant offer a Crew by itself when a request looks complex enough. It still cannot start one until you commit a configuration, and it can never grant itself more permission than you already gave.

settings.label: Crew Auto Threshold
settings.desc: How complex a request has to look before Crew Auto offers a Crew.

settings.label: Crew Auto Size Limit
settings.desc: The largest Crew that Crew Auto may propose without you raising it yourself.

settings.label: BrainStorm Participants
settings.desc: How many core thinkers a BrainStorm starts with, before optional Wonderer and Grill Me roles are added.

settings.label: BrainStorm Question Limit
settings.desc: The most questions a BrainStorm may ask you before it plans (20). Grill Me raises this by its own extension, so the Grill Me total is 45.

settings.label: Grill Me Extra Questions
settings.desc: How many additional questions Grill Me adds to a workflow's allowance (25). Questions are shared across participants, so this does not multiply per teammate.

settings.label: Quick Plan Question Limit
settings.desc: The most questions a Quick Plan may ask you before it writes the document. Grill Me raises this to 28.

settings.label: Standard Plan Question Limit
settings.desc: The most questions a Standard Plan may ask you before it writes the document. Grill Me raises this to 31.

settings.label: Thorough Plan Question Limit
settings.desc: The most questions a Thorough Plan may ask you before it writes the document. Grill Me raises this to 33.

settings.label: Deep Plan Thorough Question Limit
settings.desc: The most questions a Deep Plan Thorough run may ask you. Grill Me raises this to 35.

settings.label: Deep Plan Exhaustive Question Limit
settings.desc: The most questions a Deep Plan Exhaustive run may ask you. Grill Me raises this to 40.

settings.label: BrainStorm Research Depth
settings.desc: How hard a BrainStorm researches outside your project. It stays read-only against your code either way.

settings.label: Independent Proposals First
settings.desc: Each participant writes its own proposal before anyone sees the others, so debate starts from genuinely different positions instead of the first idea.

settings.label: BrainStorm Debate Rounds
settings.desc: How many rounds of evidence-driven debate run before voting.

settings.label: BrainStorm Voting
settings.desc: How the group decides: weighted by evidence, a plain majority, or the coordinator adjudicates.

settings.label: Keep Dissent
settings.desc: Records the positions that lost the vote in the final Plan, so a rejected option is visible rather than erased.

settings.label: Review Strategy
settings.desc: Whether Review runs one fresh reviewer or several independent passes that compare findings afterwards.

settings.label: Reviewers
settings.desc: How many independent reviewers a Multi-Pass Review uses, from one to eight. Repeating the same model is allowed and still gives independent passes.

settings.label: Blind First Pass
settings.desc: Reviewers cannot see each other's findings on the first pass, so agreement means something. They exchange findings only afterwards.

settings.label: Compare Findings
settings.desc: After the blind passes, reviewers see each other's findings and mark agreement or disagreement.

settings.label: Keep Review Dissent
settings.desc: Keeps a finding that only one reviewer stood behind, marked as disputed rather than dropped.

settings.label: Review Fixes Things
settings.desc: Off, and locked off for this feature: Review reads and reports. Acting on a finding is always a separate explicit step.

settings.label: Chat Room Size
settings.desc: How many participants a new Chat Room starts with.

settings.label: Chat Room Turns
settings.desc: How the room takes turns: moderated by one participant, strict round-robin, or free-for-all.

settings.label: Chat Room Rounds
settings.desc: How many rounds a room runs before it stops and offers a summary.

settings.label: Back Seat Driver
settings.desc: A separate read-only adviser that watches your work and raises concerns. Auto runs it on the moments that usually matter, On watches continuously, Off disables it. It never approves, changes, or certifies anything, and your work continues normally if it fails.

settings.label: Adviser Model
settings.desc: Which model the Back Seat Driver uses. Default lets the resolver pick. Its usage is billed and shown separately from your main work.

settings.label: Adviser Persona
settings.desc: Which persona the Back Seat Driver speaks as. Critical Advisor is blunt about risk.

settings.label: Adviser Sensitivity
settings.desc: How readily the adviser speaks up. Balanced raises concerns and criticals but stays quiet about nits.

settings.label: Adviser Catch-Up
settings.desc: How long the adviser may spend catching up on work that happened while it was busy, before it skips ahead to current work.

settings.label: Adviser Cooldown
settings.desc: How many turns the adviser stays quiet after speaking, so it does not repeat itself.

settings.label: Keep Adviser Transcript
settings.desc: Keeps the adviser's own conversation so you can open it and see why it said something.

settings.label: Adviser Compaction Point
settings.desc: How full the adviser's own context gets before it compacts itself. Its compaction never touches your conversation.

settings.label: Wind-Down Time
settings.desc: How long before a window closes the assistant stops taking on big new work, so the current step can finish safely instead of being cut off mid-write.

settings.label: If A Schedule Is Missed
settings.desc: What happens when a scheduled time passes while the app is closed: hold it for you, send at the next opportunity, or cancel after the grace period.

settings.label: Schedule Grace Period
settings.desc: How late a missed schedule may still run before Cancel after grace gives up on it.

settings.label: Resume Next Window
settings.desc: Picks paused work back up when the next execution window opens. A manual Stop or Pause always wins over this.

settings.label: Resume When Usage Resets
settings.desc: Off by default. When you tick the box on a paused run, it resumes once the provider's usage window reopens -- unless you stopped it yourself, which always wins.

settings.label: Daylight Saving Behavior
settings.desc: Keeps a 10 PM window at 10 PM local on both sides of a clock change, rather than drifting by an hour. The skipped and repeated hours each run exactly once.

settings.label: Screenshot Scope
settings.desc: Whether the screenshot button captures just what you can see or the whole scrolling page.

settings.label: After Picking A Component
settings.desc: What happens when you pick a component: send it straight away, add it to a numbered list in the composer, or insert it at your cursor. Remembers whichever you used last.
settings.default: Last used, starting with Send now
settings.recommended: Last used, starting with Send now

settings.label: Include Component Image
settings.desc: Attaches a cropped picture of the component alongside its structure and styles.

settings.label: Agent DevTools Access
settings.desc: Whether the assistant may open DevTools in the ordinary internal browser. The protected sign-in browser is never included and stays yours alone.
